From an information-theoretic perspective, we present a key insight: effective detection in the low-level statistical space requires mitigating the dominance of semantic components while emphasizing and amplifying responses to low-SNR forgery traces. Building on this insight, we propose RippleNet, an AI-generated image detection framework based on local differential signals. RippleNet adaptively identifies forgery-sensitive regions and constructs multi-directional, multi-scale differential representations within local neighborhoods, explicitly characterizing anomalous patterns in neighborhood statistics. More importantly, we refine the attention mechanism to operate within the local differential representation space, enabling the model to establish explicit dependencies at a finer statistical granularity. This design facilitates the capture of pixel-level forgery traces that are difficult to model using conventional convolutions or image-wide patch-level attention. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks and under cross-generator evaluation settings demonstrate that RippleNet achieves consistently competitive performance.

AI.tldr: RippleNet is an AI-generated image detection framework that uses local differential signals to amplify low-SNR forensic cues, overcoming the dominance of semantically salient features during training, and achieves competitive performance across public benchmarks and cross-generator settings.
AI.motivation: Existing detection methods are dominated by semantically salient components with high signal-to-noise ratios during training, which suppresses subtle low-level forensic cues embedded in the statistical structures of generated images. The paper identifies from an information-theoretic perspective that effective detection requires mitigating semantic dominance and amplifying low-SNR forgery traces.
AI.method: RippleNet is a detection framework based on local differential signals. It adaptively identifies forgery-sensitive regions and constructs multi-directional, multi-scale differential representations within local neighborhoods to characterize anomalous patterns in neighborhood statistics. It also refines attention mechanisms to operate in the local differential representation space, capturing pixel-level forgery traces at finer statistical granularity.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks and under cross-generator evaluation settings demonstrate that RippleNet achieves consistently competitive performance.
AI.conclusion: RippleNet effectively addresses the semantic dominance problem in AI-generated image detection by emphasizing low-level differential forensic signals, and provides a robust approach for detecting forged images including those from unseen generators.

title: LocusGS: Spatially Grounded Tokens for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Recent query-based feed-forward 3DGS methods represent a scene using learnable queries, each aggregating multi-view evidence and decoding a group of Gaussians. Ideally, different queries should specialize in coherent local regions of the scene. However, we observe that Gaussians decoded from the same query often scatter across distant scene regions, resulting in weak query-level spatial coherence and poor alignment with the scene structure. We attribute this behavior to the purely latent representation of existing Gaussian queries. To address this limitation, we introduce LocusGS, which augments each Gaussian query with a 3D anchor state consisting of a center and a support radius. The anchor state is progressively refined across decoder layers and is used throughout query interaction, multi-view feature aggregation, and Gaussian generation. Specifically, an anchor-to-ray geometric bias guides each query toward spatially relevant image observations, while anchor-centered decoding organizes its Gaussians within a local region. Experiments on novel view synthesis benchmarks show that LocusGS improves rendering quality over query-based Gaussian token baselines under the same Gaussian budget. Further analysis shows that the learned anchors form coherent spatial layouts and lead to more structured Gaussian distributions, demonstrating that explicit anchor states improve the spatial organization. Our project page: https://leo-frank.github.io/LocusGS_viewer.

AI.tldr: LocusGS is a query-based feed-forward 3DGS method that augments each Gaussian query with an explicit 3D anchor state (center and support radius) to improve spatial coherence, enabling Gaussians decoded from the same query to stay within local scene regions and improving rendering quality on novel view synthesis benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing query-based feed-forward 3DGS methods rely on purely latent query representations, causing Gaussians decoded from the same query to scatter across distant scene regions, resulting in weak query-level spatial coherence and poor alignment with the scene structure.
AI.method: LocusGS augments each Gaussian query with a 3D anchor state consisting of a center and a support radius. The anchor state is progressively refined across decoder layers and used throughout query interaction, multi-view feature aggregation, and Gaussian generation. It employs an anchor-to-ray geometric bias to guide queries toward spatially relevant image observations, and anchor-centered decoding to organize Gaussians within local regions.
AI.result: Experiments on novel view synthesis benchmarks show LocusGS improves rendering quality over query-based Gaussian token baselines under the same Gaussian budget. Analysis demonstrates that learned anchors form coherent spatial layouts and lead to more structured Gaussian distributions.
AI.conclusion: Explicit anchor states improve the spatial organization of query-based 3DGS methods, addressing the weak spatial coherence problem in existing latent-query approaches.

title: Validation of Smartphone-Based Photogrammetric 3D Body Scanning for Automated Anthropometric Measurements Compared with a Commercial Depth-Sensor-Based Body Scanner
summary: 3D body scanning has become an important tool in healthcare applications because of its rapid and non-invasive nature. While smartphone-based photogrammetric reconstruction provide a low-cost and accessible alternative to commercial 3D body scanners, their performance for whole-body scanning remains insufficiently validated. Thus, we designed this study to comprehensively validate the photogrammetric 3D scanning application by evaluating automatically extracted whole-body measurements and longitudinal body-shape monitoring. We evaluated a representative application, PolyCam, against the commercial depth-sensor-based Fit3D ProScanner using 144 pregnant participants scanned longitudinally throughout pregnancy. We designed an automatic circumference extraction pipeline to get measurements at four anatomical landmarks from paired 3D scans. A linear mixed-effects model was used to evaluate scanner effects and longitudinal body-shape changes. Measurement consistency was assessed using repeated PolyCam scans and tape measurements on a rigid mannequin. PolyCam demonstrated strong agreement with Fit3D, with average biases below 16 mm, intraclass correlation coefficients above 0.8, and Pearson correlation coefficients above 0.9 across all landmarks. Both systems captured comparable longitudinal body-shape changes. Mannequin experiments showed mean biases below 3.5 mm and no significant differences from tape measurements. These findings support smartphone photogrammetry as a potential accessible alternative to commercial body scanners and applicable for longitudinal 3D body-shape assessment.

AI.tldr: This study validates smartphone-based photogrammetric 3D body scanning (using PolyCam) against a commercial depth-sensor scanner (Fit3D ProScanner) with 144 pregnant participants scanned longitudinally. Results show strong agreement (biases <16mm, ICC>0.8, Pearson>0.9), comparable longitudinal body-shape tracking, and high accuracy on mannequin tests, supporting smartphone photogrammetry as an accessible alternative for whole-body scanning.
AI.motivation: Smartphone-based photogrammetric reconstruction offers a low-cost, accessible alternative to commercial 3D body scanners, but its performance for whole-body scanning, particularly for longitudinal monitoring, has not been sufficiently validated.
AI.method: The study evaluated the PolyCam application against Fit3D ProScanner using 144 pregnant participants scanned longitudinally. An automatic circumference extraction pipeline was designed to obtain measurements at four anatomical landmarks from paired 3D scans. A linear mixed-effects model assessed scanner effects and longitudinal body-shape changes. Consistency was validated using repeated PolyCam scans and tape measurements on a rigid mannequin.
AI.result: PolyCam showed strong agreement with Fit3D with average biases below 16 mm, ICC above 0.8, and Pearson correlations above 0.9 across all landmarks. Both systems captured comparable longitudinal body-shape changes. Mannequin experiments showed mean biases below 3.5 mm with no significant differences from tape measurements.
AI.conclusion: Smartphone photogrammetry is a viable accessible alternative to commercial body scanners and is applicable for longitudinal 3D body-shape assessment in healthcare settings.

title: Semantic Steering for Controllable Generation: Tuning-Free Concept Erasure in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
summary: Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) have demonstrated remarkable text-to-image generation performance, surpassing traditional U-Net-based diffusion models. Nevertheless, their powerful generative capabilities also raise significant safety concerns, as they may generate sensitive or inappropriate content. While existing concept erasure methods aim to mitigate such risks, most require modifying model parameters, which are often architecture-specific and impractical for deployed larger models. Several tuning-free approaches face challenges when applied to advanced large-scale MM-DiTs due to their deeply embedded knowledge, broad semantic space, and context-dependent text encoders. To address these challenges, we propose to erase concepts by directly manipulating the model's internal representations. Our key insight, derived from an in-depth analysis of MM-DiT's block-wise generative roles, is that text-conditioned semantic representations are most salient in the middle blocks of MM-DiTs. Based on this, we extract representations of an unwanted concept and a desirable safe one from the middle block, construct a steering vector from their difference, and inject this single vector into consecutive early and middle blocks. By operating exclusively on the sparse text-branch tokens and leveraging the straight sampling trajectory of rectified flow, our method achieves effective concept erasure with negligible overhead and without any training. Extensive experiments across MM-DiT models demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in erasing diverse concepts, enables effective control over the final output, and remains robust to adversarial attacks.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a training-free concept erasure method for Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs) by directly manipulating the model's internal representations. The key insight is that text-conditioned semantic representations are most salient in the middle blocks of MM-DiTs; the method extracts representations of unwanted and safe concepts from the middle block, constructs a steering vector from their difference, and injects it into early and middle blocks via sparse text-branch tokens.
AI.motivation: While MM-DiTs achieve superior text-to-image generation, their powerful generative capabilities raise safety concerns. Existing concept erasure methods either require architecture-specific parameter modifications impractical for deployed large models, or tuning-free approaches that struggle with advanced large-scale MM-DiTs due to deeply embedded knowledge, broad semantic space, and context-dependent text encoders.
AI.method: The method (1) analyzes MM-DiT's block-wise generative roles to identify that text-conditioned semantic representations are most salient in middle blocks; (2) extracts representations of an unwanted concept and a safe concept from the middle block; (3) constructs a steering vector from their difference; (4) injects this single vector into consecutive early and middle blocks, operating exclusively on sparse text-branch tokens and leveraging rectified flow's straight sampling trajectory. No training is required.
AI.result: Experiments across MM-DiT models demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in erasing diverse concepts, effective control over final output, and robustness to adversarial attacks, all achieved with negligible overhead.
AI.conclusion: Direct internal representation manipulation, specifically using steering vectors derived from difference of concept representations in middle blocks, offers an effective, training-free, and architecture-agnostic approach to concept erasure in large-scale MM-DiTs.

title: Heterogeneous Vision-Language Ensemble with Disagreement-Aware Reranking for Text-Based Person Anomaly Retrieval
summary: Text-based person anomaly retrieval aims to retrieve pedestrians exhibiting anomalous behaviors from a large image gallery using natural language descriptions. Compared with conventional text-based person retrieval, this task requires fine-grained reasoning over pedestrian appearance, behaviors, object interactions, and scene context, making robust cross-modal matching significantly more challenging. This paper presents the GENAI4E team's solution to AI City Challenge 2026 Track 4. Our framework builds upon a strong retrieval backbone and progressively integrates heterogeneous vision-language embedding models through score alignment and iterative ensemble fusion, followed by disagreement-aware VLM reranking for ambiguous queries. On the official Pedestrian Anomaly Behavior (PAB) benchmark, our approach achieves 90.92% mAP, 85.13% Recall@1, 97.72% Recall@5, and 98.68% Recall@10, demonstrating the effectiveness of combining complementary vision-language representations with selective multimodal reasoning for large-scale text-based person anomaly retrieval.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the GENAI4E team's solution for AI City Challenge 2026 Track 4 on text-based person anomaly retrieval. The framework combines heterogeneous vision-language embedding models via score alignment and iterative ensemble fusion, followed by disagreement-aware VLM reranking. It achieves 90.92% mAP, 85.13% Recall@1, 97.72% Recall@5, and 98.68% Recall@10 on the PAB benchmark.
AI.motivation: Text-based person anomaly retrieval is more challenging than conventional text-based person retrieval because it requires fine-grained reasoning over pedestrian appearance, behaviors, object interactions, and scene context, making robust cross-modal matching significantly difficult.
AI.method: The framework uses a strong retrieval backbone, progressively integrates heterogeneous vision-language embedding models through score alignment and iterative ensemble fusion, and applies disagreement-aware VLM reranking for ambiguous queries.
AI.result: The approach achieves 90.92% mAP, 85.13% Recall@1, 97.72% Recall@5, and 98.68% Recall@10 on the official Pedestrian Anomaly Behavior (PAB) benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining complementary vision-language representations with selective multimodal reasoning for large-scale text-based person anomaly retrieval.

title: SPARED: Reasoning-Based AI-Generated Image Detection via Adversarially Edited Data
summary: Detecting AI-generated images is only half the task: a deployed detector must also justify its verdict, yet existing detectors inherit three failure modes from their training data: real and fake images collected from different sources invite provenance shortcuts, supervised explanation corpora teach templated rationales, and a static forgery corpus leaves the decision boundary standing still while generators keep moving. We introduce \methodname{}, an adversarial reinforcement learning framework that pits two heterogeneous models against each other. A diffusion image editor learns to edit real photographs into fake counterparts of those same photographs that fool the current detector, while a reasoning MLLM learns to expose them with a verdict grounded in free-form reasoning. Both rewards are shortcut-proof by design: the attacker is credited only when its edit is faithfully executed, and the defender only when its verdict is correct. As the two models alternate, each round's attacker regenerates a harder training pool aimed at the current detector's blind spots, so the detector must generalize rather than memorize any fixed artifact distribution. Although the explanation is never rewarded, its quality rises round over round as a side effect of accuracy-only training. A detector trained within this loop improves monotonically across rounds on each of three external benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Introduces an adversarial reinforcement learning framework where a diffusion-based image editor generates fake images targeting a detector's blind spots while a reasoning MLLM detects them with free-form justifications, improving both detection accuracy and explanation quality across rounds.
AI.motivation: Existing AI-image detectors fail in deployment because their training data introduces three issues: provenance shortcuts from mismatched real/fake sources, templated rationales from supervised explanation corpora, and a static forgery corpus that leaves detectors behind as generators evolve. A deployed detector must not only detect but justify its verdict, which current approaches cannot reliably do.
AI.method: The framework pits two heterogeneous models in adversarial RL: (1) a diffusion image editor that edits real photographs into fake counterparts fooling the current detector, rewarded only when edits are faithfully executed; and (2) a reasoning MLLM that detects fakes with free-form reasoning, rewarded only when verdicts are correct. Alternating rounds regenerate harder training pools targeting detector blind spots, forcing generalization over memorization.
AI.result: The detector trained within the loop improves monotonically across rounds on three external benchmarks. Although explanations are never directly rewarded, their quality improves round over round as a side effect of accuracy-only training.
AI.conclusion: Adversarial co-training between a generative attacker and a reasoning defender produces shortcut-proof detectors with improving free-form explanations, addressing all three failure modes of static, sourced training corpora.

title: NaviDC-OCR: Navigating Document Parsing Across Digital and Camera-Captured Documents
summary: Document parsing aims to transform unstructured documents into structured and machine-readable representations. Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have significantly advanced document parsing. However, existing approaches still face two major challenges. First, decoupled VLM-based methods heavily rely on accurate layout analysis, where geometric distortions in camera-captured documents can introduce cascading errors. Second, although end-to-end VLM-based methods alleviate the dependence on explicit layout detection, they often suffer from redundant generation, hallucinations, and insufficient structural reasoning in high-resolution scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose NaviDC-OCR, a unified framework for document parsing. NaviDC-OCR introduces deformation-aware learning to incorporate geometric perception into VLMs and proposes an adaptive sampling mechanism for complex layout representation. Furthermore, a content-structure decoupled learning strategy is developed to explicitly model formula grammars and table structures, enabling more effective structured representation learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that NaviDC-OCR achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse document parsing benchmarks. It obtains overall scores of 96.87, 88.53 and 78.41 on OmniDocBench v1.6, Wild-OmniDocBench, and PureDocBench, respectively, and ranks first in the ICDAR 2026 Sci-ImageMiner Challenge. These results validate the effectiveness and generalization capability of NaviDC-OCR in complex document parsing scenarios.

AI.tldr: NaviDC-OCR is a unified VLM-based framework for document parsing that addresses geometric distortions in camera-captured documents and structural reasoning limitations through deformation-aware learning, adaptive sampling, and content-structure decoupled learning, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing document parsing methods face two major challenges: (1) decoupled VLM-based approaches heavily depend on accurate layout analysis, where geometric distortions in camera-captured documents cause cascading errors, and (2) end-to-end VLM-based methods suffer from redundant generation, hallucinations, and insufficient structural reasoning in high-resolution scenarios.
AI.method: NaviDC-OCR proposes three key components: (1) deformation-aware learning to incorporate geometric perception into VLMs, (2) an adaptive sampling mechanism for complex layout representation, and (3) a content-structure decoupled learning strategy to explicitly model formula grammars and table structures.
AI.result: NaviDC-OCR achieves state-of-the-art performance with overall scores of 96.87 on OmniDocBench v1.6, 88.53 on Wild-OmniDocBench, and 78.41 on PureDocBench, and ranks first in the ICDAR 2026 Sci-ImageMiner Challenge.
AI.conclusion: The results validate that NaviDC-OCR effectively handles complex document parsing scenarios, demonstrating strong generalization capability across diverse benchmarks and real-world challenges such as geometric distortion, complex layouts, and structured content like formulas and tables.

title: HounsWorld: A Multimodal World Model for Hidden Patient-State Readout, Reconstruction, and Simulation
summary: Clinical intelligence requires estimating a patient's underlying condition from incomplete observations rather than learning isolated mappings from scans to answers. Volumetric medical images provide dense observations of anatomy, attenuation, and lesions, whereas clinical language provides sparse but complementary semantic observations. We formulate CT-centered intelligence as inference over a shared latent patient state, under which readout, reconstruction, and simulation all become state-dependent prediction problems. To operationalize this view, we introduce HounsBench, a computed tomography (CT) centric patient-state benchmark that unifies these three task families with patient-disjoint splits and per-family metrics, and HounsWorld, a 3B multimodal world model that treats volumetric scans and language as observations of the shared state through Joint Understanding-Generation Learning. A shared transformer forms an implicit patient-state estimate and supports three outputs: query-conditioned answers that read out the state, reports and captions that reconstruct it in language, and condition-specific CT volumes for low-dose denoising, virtual contrast enhancement, and anatomy-constrained text-and-mask-to-volume generation. Zero-initialized CT adapters preserve pretrained multimodal mappings, while condition-explicit Hounsfield-unit window sampling exposes clinically meaningful density observations. HounsWorld shows strong performance across all three task families while consistently improving CT understanding through clinically structured completion. Our project is available at https://github.com/byhwhite/HounsWorld.git

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a unified framework for CT-centered clinical intelligence, treating volumetric medical images and clinical language as complementary observations of a shared latent patient state. It presents HounsBench, a benchmark unifying readout, reconstruction, and simulation tasks, and HounsWorld, a 3B multimodal world model using Joint Understanding-Generation Learning to perform all three task families through a shared transformer with zero-initialized CT adapters and Hounsfield-unit window sampling.
AI.motivation: Clinical intelligence requires estimating a patient's underlying condition from incomplete observations rather than learning isolated mappings from scans to answers. Volumetric medical images provide dense observations while clinical language provides sparse but complementary semantic observations, motivating a unified patient-state inference framework.
AI.method: Formulates CT-centered intelligence as inference over a shared latent patient state, implemented as HounsWorld, a 3B multimodal world model. It treats volumetric scans and language as observations of the shared state through Joint Understanding-Generation Learning, using a shared transformer with query-conditioned readout, language reconstruction, and condition-specific CT volume generation. Zero-initialized CT adapters preserve pretrained multimodal mappings, and condition-explicit Hounsfield-unit window sampling exposes clinically meaningful density observations.
AI.result: HounsWorld demonstrates strong performance across readout, reconstruction, and simulation task families (including low-dose denoising, virtual contrast enhancement, and text-and-mask-to-volume generation), while consistently improving CT understanding through clinically structured completion.
AI.conclusion: A unified patient-state modeling approach effectively integrates volumetric and language observations, improving performance across multiple CT-centered clinical tasks simultaneously, with the code released publicly.

title: Beyond Visual Evidence: Revealing and Mitigating Relational Privacy Leakage in Document MLLMs
summary: While the privacy risks of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have drawn significant attention, the unique vulnerabilities of domain-specific MLLMs remain largely underexplored. Focusing on document understanding MLLMs for identity document processing, this paper investigates the privacy issues inherent in Key Information Extraction (KIE) tasks. We reveal that when input images lack sufficient visual evidence, these models often rely on memorized field relations from training data to infer missing content, thereby leaking multiple correlated fields containing sensitive personal information. To mitigate this risk, we make three key contributions.First, we propose the Dynamic Relational Unlearning Framework (DRUF) which comprises a Relational Decoupling Unlearning (RDU) module and a dynamic set update mechanism. It suppresses the leakage of high-risk field pairs while preserving KIE performance.Second, we introduce DocPrivacyBench, a novel benchmark to systematically evaluate a model's susceptibility to privacy leakage under conditions of absent or minimal visual evidence.Third, we evaluate three MLLMs and six unlearning methods using this benchmark, assessing both post-unlearning leakage suppression and utility preservation.Our results demonstrate that existing MLLMs consistently exhibit privacy leakage when visual evidence is scarce, particularly on noisier datasets. In contrast, DRUF outperforms the strongest baseline by improving leakage suppression by 4.8 percentage points, effectively mitigating privacy risks while maintaining robust document information extraction performance.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates privacy leakage in document understanding multimodal large language models (MLLMs) used for identity document Key Information Extraction (KIE). It reveals that models infer missing content from memorized field relations when visual evidence is scarce, leaking correlated sensitive fields. The authors propose DRUF (Dynamic Relational Unlearning Framework) to suppress high-risk field pair leakage while preserving KIE performance, and introduce DocPrivacyBench, a benchmark for evaluating privacy susceptibility. Experiments show DRUF outperforms the strongest baseline by 4.8 percentage points in leakage suppression.
AI.motivation: While privacy risks of general MLLMs have been studied, the unique vulnerabilities of domain-specific MLLMs (particularly document understanding models for identity document processing) remain underexplored. The paper aims to fill this gap by studying privacy leakage in KIE tasks.
AI.method: The paper proposes DRUF (Dynamic Relational Unlearning Framework) comprising a Relational Decoupling Unlearning (RDU) module and a dynamic set update mechanism to suppress high-risk field pair leakage. It also introduces DocPrivacyBench, a benchmark for evaluating privacy susceptibility under absent or minimal visual evidence conditions.
AI.result: Existing MLLMs consistently exhibit privacy leakage when visual evidence is scarce, particularly on noisier datasets. DRUF outperforms the strongest baseline by improving leakage suppression by 4.8 percentage points while maintaining robust KIE performance.
AI.conclusion: DRUF effectively mitigates privacy risks in document understanding MLLMs while preserving document information extraction performance, and DocPrivacyBench provides a systematic evaluation framework for privacy leakage susceptibility.

title: TennisVAR: A Stroke-Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Large Language Model for Tactical Reasoning in Tennis Videos
summary: Sports-video understanding is moving beyond event recognition toward explaining how actions collectively shape match progression, however, existing tennis-video methods either perceive individual strokes without modeling their tactical dependencies or generate high-level analyses without grounding them in the underlying events. To bridge this perception-to-understanding gap, we formulate stroke-evidence-grounded tactical reasoning, a new rally-level task that requires models to jointly predict an open-ended answer, a hierarchical tactic label, an ordered sequence of supporting strokes, and decisive key actions, with each evidence stroke anchored to its racket-ball contact frame. We further introduce TRACE (Tactical Reasoning with Action-Chain Evidence in Tennis), a large-scale expert-annotated benchmark containing 11,189 rally videos, 41,485 stroke events, 25,429 tactical units, and 11,189 question-answer pairs, which unifies fine-grained stroke attributes, cross-stroke tactical relations, hierarchical tactic annotations, and evidence-grounded questions across factual perception, tactical understanding, and decision reasoning. Building on TRACE, we propose TennisVAR (Tennis Video Action-chain Reasoner), an evidence-grounded multimodal large language model that follows an "event-relation-evidence-tactic" reasoning paradigm, where an Event Parsing Module converts continuous rallies into explicit stroke-event sequences while a Tactical Graph-Guided Temporal Reasoner jointly models rally progression and same-player decision dependencies to identify question-relevant evidence and decisive actions.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces TRACE, a large-scale expert-annotated benchmark for tennis tactical reasoning, and TennisVAR, an evidence-grounded multimodal LLM that jointly predicts answers, tactic labels, supporting strokes, and key actions while grounding each evidence stroke in racket-ball contact frames.
AI.motivation: Existing tennis-video methods either recognize individual strokes without modeling tactical dependencies between them, or generate high-level analyses without grounding them in the underlying events. There is a gap between low-level perception (stroke detection) and high-level understanding (tactical reasoning), which this paper aims to bridge via a new rally-level task formulation.
AI.method: The paper proposes a new task, stroke-evidence-grounded tactical reasoning, requiring joint prediction of an open-ended answer, hierarchical tactic label, ordered supporting stroke sequence, and decisive key actions. It introduces TRACE benchmark (11,189 rally videos, 41,485 stroke events, 25,429 tactical units, 11,189 QA pairs) and TennisVAR, an evidence-grounded MLLM following an "event-relation-evidence-tactic" paradigm with an Event Parsing Module and a Tactical Graph-Guided Temporal Reasoner.
AI.result: The paper presents the TRACE benchmark and TennisVAR model, though specific quantitative results are not reported in the abstract. The contribution is primarily the task formulation, benchmark construction, and model architecture design.
AI.conclusion: The proposed TRACE benchmark and TennisVAR model address the perception-to-understanding gap in sports video analysis by grounding high-level tactical reasoning in explicit stroke-level evidence, enabling fine-grained and interpretable analysis of how individual actions shape match progression.

title: A Deep RL based Framework for Targeted White Matter Tractography
summary:
Fiber tractography's ability to reconstruct the brain's structural pathways, has made it a crucial component of modern neuroimaging, enabling detailed, non-invasive mapping of structural connectivity and supporting a wide range of neurological research and clinical applications. However, despite its importance, tractography remains a challenging task due to the inherent complexity of white matter structure and its susceptibility to false positives, which can lead to the misrepresentation of critical pathways.
  To overcome these limitations, in this thesis, we propose a hybrid framework that integrates reinforcement learning with supervised learning for refining RL policies, specifically tailored for tract-specific tractography. Notably, our framework does not rely on ground-truth fibers for training. Moreover, the tract-specific formulation bypasses the need for an explicit segmentation process, simplifying the overall pipeline.
  Our work includes two main contributions, each building upon the previous. First, we introduce a hybrid approach that combines reinforcement learning with supervised learning (specifically, GPT-based policy learning) to refine policies in a tract-specific context. Second, we propose a scalable framework for data-driven multi-policy fusion, which leverages the complementary strengths of multiple RL policies to improve tractography performance and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework through extensive validation on benchmark public datasets including TractoInferno, HCP, and ISMRM-2015, highlighting its ability to generalize across data sources and accurately reconstruct brain white matter tracts. We believe that these contributions represent significant advancements in the field of tractography, improving robustness, reliability, and accuracy while reducing dependence on ground-truth annotations.

AI.tldr: This thesis proposes a hybrid reinforcement learning and supervised learning (GPT-based) framework for tract-specific fiber tractography that does not rely on ground-truth fibers, and introduces a scalable multi-policy fusion approach to improve tractography accuracy and robustness across multiple public datasets.
AI.motivation: Fiber tractography is essential for mapping brain structural connectivity but suffers from false positives and the inherent complexity of white matter structure, leading to misrepresentation of critical pathways. Existing methods often depend on ground-truth fibers and explicit segmentation processes, limiting their reliability and generalizability.
AI.method: The framework integrates reinforcement learning with supervised learning (specifically GPT-based policy learning) to refine RL policies for tract-specific tractography. It avoids ground-truth fiber dependence and bypasses explicit segmentation. Two contributions: (1) a hybrid RL+supervised learning approach for policy refinement; (2) a scalable data-driven multi-policy fusion framework that combines multiple RL policies to enhance performance and robustness.
AI.result: Extensive validation on benchmark datasets including TractoInferno, HCP, and ISMRM-2015 demonstrates the framework's ability to generalize across diverse data sources and accurately reconstruct brain white matter tracts.
AI.conclusion: The proposed contributions represent significant advancements in tractography, improving robustness, reliability, and accuracy while reducing dependence on ground-truth annotations.

title: Bias Mitigation in Face Recognition via Demographic-based Supervised Contrastive Learning
summary: Face recognition systems have been shown to be biased toward certain demographic groups by exhibiting different error rates across gender, age, or ethnicity. Though the imbalance of the training data with respect to these demographics is one cause of this bias, training on artificially balanced groups does not completely mitigate the problem. For deployment, face recognition typically works at operating points allowing very low false match rates and, hence, on the tail of the non-match score distribution. While class balancing can improve the means of these distributions, the aim of our approach is to improve fairness by addressing the behavior in the tail. Particularly, we propose the Demographic-based Supervised Contrastive loss (DeSCon) for face recognition, which relies on a well-designed composition of training batches and demographic-aware pair selection. Our experimental evaluation on both demographically-labeled datasets and standard verification benchmarks shows that DeSCon can improve fairness beyond balancing training datasets while maintaining competitive verification performance. Source code is available upon request.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes DeSCon (Demographic-based Supervised Contrastive loss) for fair face recognition. Unlike class balancing which improves mean error distributions, DeSCon targets the tail of the non-match score distribution to improve fairness across demographic groups while maintaining competitive verification performance.
AI.motivation: Face recognition systems exhibit demographic bias with different error rates across gender, age, or ethnicity. While training data imbalance contributes to this bias, simply balancing training data does not fully resolve it. Since face recognition operates at very low false match rates (the tail of the non-match score distribution), fairness improvements need to address the tail behavior rather than just the means.
AI.method: The paper proposes the Demographic-based Supervised Contrastive loss (DeSCon), which uses a well-designed composition of training batches and demographic-aware pair selection to improve fairness by addressing the behavior in the tail of the non-match score distribution.
AI.result: Experimental evaluation on demographically-labeled datasets and standard verification benchmarks shows that DeSCon improves fairness beyond what balancing training datasets achieves, while maintaining competitive verification performance.
AI.conclusion: Demographic-aware contrastive learning that targets the tail of score distributions can improve fairness in face recognition beyond simply balancing training data, without sacrificing verification accuracy.

title: DiCoR: Decoupled Referent Disambiguation and Contour Recalibration for Efficient Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
summary: Referring remote sensing image segmentation (RRSIS) aims to delineate targets specified by natural language expressions in remote sensing imagery. Existing methods mainly follow joint fusion segmentation (JFS) or decoupled prompt segmentation (DPS). JFS is efficient but often suffers from limited accuracy because referent localization and mask delineation are optimized under a unified objective, whereas DPS separates localization from mask generation using spatial prompts and foundation segmenters at the cost of higher memory consumption and inference latency. To bridge this gap, we propose DiCoR, a decoupled referent disambiguation and contour recalibration framework built on an efficient JFS pipeline. DiCoR addresses two key challenges: distinguishing the correct referent from ambiguous candidates and refining coarse masks after localization. A disambiguation-aware localization guidance strategy ranks salient candidate regions with adaptive linguistic cues and injects the resulting localization prior into fused features. A lightweight contour recalibration module further predicts residual corrections to coarse logits under localized contour supervision, improving mask quality with limited computational overhead. Experiments on RefSegRS, RRSIS-D, and RISBench show that DiCoR achieves the best segmentation accuracy across all three benchmarks. On RefSegRS, it improves mIoU and gIoU by 5.28% and 2.87% over a competitive JFS method while running 4.7% faster than a representative DPS method, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. Code is available at https://github.com/zyGao1126/DiCoR.

AI.tldr: DiCoR is a decoupled referent disambiguation and contour recalibration framework for referring remote sensing image segmentation (RRSIS), built on an efficient joint fusion segmentation pipeline. It uses a disambiguation-aware localization guidance strategy to rank salient candidates with adaptive linguistic cues and a lightweight contour recalibration module to refine coarse masks. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on RefSegRS, RRSIS-D, and RISBench with a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
AI.motivation: Existing RRSIS methods fall into two categories with complementary limitations: JFS is efficient but suffers from limited accuracy due to unified optimization of localization and mask delineation, while DPS achieves better separation but incurs higher memory and inference latency. The paper aims to bridge this accuracy-efficiency gap.
AI.method: DiCoR consists of two key components: (1) a disambiguation-aware localization guidance strategy that ranks salient candidate regions using adaptive linguistic cues and injects the resulting localization prior into fused features to distinguish the correct referent from ambiguous candidates; and (2) a lightweight contour recalibration module that predicts residual corrections to coarse logits under localized contour supervision to improve mask quality with minimal computational overhead.
AI.result: DiCoR achieves the best segmentation accuracy across RefSegRS, RRSIS-D, and RISBench. On RefSegRS, it improves mIoU and gIoU by 5.28% and 2.87% over a competitive JFS method while running 4.7% faster than a representative DPS method.
AI.conclusion: DiCoR demonstrates that decoupled referent disambiguation and contour recalibration can be effectively integrated into an efficient JFS pipeline, achieving a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off and establishing a new state of the art in RRSIS.

title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels
summary: Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) enables text-to-3D generation by optimizing rendered images with a pretrained diffusion prior, but latent SDS often produces structured color artifacts and high-frequency texture noise. We identify a failure mode of latent SDS caused by VAE-induced pixel drift: the optimized image can move along pixel-space directions that are weakly constrained by the VAE encoder, so its latent representation remains clean and semantically meaningful while the image itself accumulates visible artifacts. We support this diagnosis with controlled 2D SDS experiments, VAE-only optimization, and a simplified analysis showing that encoder-like latent objectives can amplify image-space noise when the inverse mapping to pixels is underconstrained. Motivated by this observation, we propose PixSDS, a lightweight VAE-consistent gradient repair method. PixSDS decodes a latent SDS lookahead step and uses the decoded image as a clean direction for pixel-space optimization, reducing motion in VAE-inconsistent directions without retraining the diffusion model, changing the renderer, or replacing the SDS objective. Experiments in 2D optimization and text-to-3D generation show that PixSDS substantially reduces structured artifacts while preserving semantic content. Code is publicly available at https://sevashasla.github.io/pixsds-webpage/.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a failure mode in latent Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) for text-to-3D generation caused by VAE-induced pixel drift, where images accumulate artifacts in pixel-space directions weakly constrained by the VAE encoder. The authors propose PixSDS, a lightweight gradient repair method that decodes the latent SDS lookahead step and uses the decoded image as a clean pixel-space optimization direction, reducing artifacts without retraining or changing the SDS objective.
AI.motivation: Latent SDS for text-to-3D generation produces structured color artifacts and high-frequency texture noise. The authors aim to diagnose the root cause of these artifacts and propose a fix that does not require retraining the diffusion model or modifying the renderer.
AI.method: The authors first diagnose the failure mode through controlled 2D SDS experiments, VAE-only optimization, and a simplified theoretical analysis showing that encoder-like latent objectives amplify image-space noise when the pixel-to-latent inverse mapping is underconstrained. They then propose PixSDS, which decodes a latent SDS lookahead step and uses the decoded image as a clean direction for pixel-space optimization to reduce motion in VAE-inconsistent directions.
AI.result: Experiments in 2D optimization and text-to-3D generation show that PixSDS substantially reduces structured artifacts while preserving semantic content, without retraining the diffusion model, changing the renderer, or replacing the SDS objective.
AI.conclusion: VAE-induced pixel drift is a key failure cause of latent SDS, and PixSDS provides an effective, lightweight repair that improves generation quality while maintaining the original pipeline's flexibility.

title: Structure-aware Riemannian Growth Fields for 4D Plant Modeling
summary: In this paper, we introduce a novel framework for 4D plant growth modeling that reconstructs the continuous geometric and topological evolution of plants from sparse temporal observations. Existing methods mainly rely on dense registration, yet reliable dense sequences are hard to obtain due to scanning constraints and self-occlusions, leaving these approaches struggling under large temporal gaps where rapid organ emergence violates local rigidity. To overcome this, we bridge these gaps by formulating plant morphogenesis as a continuous procedural process on a structure-aware Riemannian growth field; this jointly models topology evolution and geometric deformation, preserving botanical hierarchies and stable spatio-temporal correspondences across distant timepoints. Our key idea is to ground symbolic growth rules within a continuous geodesic flow, where organ development follows biologically modulated trajectories that preserve structural coherence under topological changes. We further contribute a 10-day dual-species dataset with dense geometric and semantic annotations. Experiments demonstrate that our method accurately tracks individual organ growth over time and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both geometric accuracy and correspondence consistency.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel framework for 4D plant growth modeling that reconstructs continuous geometric and topological evolution from sparse temporal observations by treating morphogenesis as a continuous procedural process on a structure-aware Riemannian growth field, jointly modeling topology evolution and geometric deformation while grounding symbolic growth rules in a continuous geodesic flow. It also contributes a 10-day dual-species dataset with dense annotations and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: Existing 4D plant growth modeling methods rely heavily on dense registration, but reliable dense temporal sequences are difficult to obtain due to scanning constraints and self-occlusions. These methods struggle under large temporal gaps where rapid organ emergence violates local rigidity assumptions, motivating the need for an approach that can bridge these gaps without requiring dense correspondence.
AI.method: The proposed framework formulates plant morphogenesis as a continuous procedural process defined on a structure-aware Riemannian growth field. This formulation jointly models topology evolution and geometric deformation, preserving botanical hierarchies and stable spatio-temporal correspondences. Symbolic growth rules are grounded within a continuous geodesic flow, where organ development follows biologically modulated trajectories that maintain structural coherence under topological changes.
AI.result: Experiments show the method accurately tracks individual organ growth over time and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both geometric accuracy and correspondence consistency. The paper also contributes a 10-day dual-species dataset with dense geometric and semantic annotations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Riemannian growth field framework effectively overcomes the limitations of dense registration-based approaches for 4D plant growth modeling, enabling robust reconstruction under large temporal gaps and topological changes while maintaining structural coherence.

title: EgoPHI: Estimating Contact and Force from Egocentric Vision
summary: Understanding hand-object interaction from egocentric vision is essential for modeling how people physically engage with the surrounding world. Yet reasoning about physically grounded interaction requires estimating the forces acting on hands and objects, beyond localizing contact. We present EgoPHI, the first method that jointly estimates dense contact maps and 3D force distributions on hand and object meshes from a single monocular RGB image and object geometry. To address the lack of scalable ground-truth force annotations, we introduce a physics-based simulation pipeline that augments existing hand-object datasets with dense per-vertex force supervision. EgoPHI then learns dense 3D contact and force on interacting hand and articulated object meshes, extending vision-based force estimation beyond image-space or planar settings. Our evaluation on in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks shows that EgoPHI improves force estimation over existing approaches while generalizing to unseen datasets. To evaluate sim-to-real transfer, we constructed two physical objects that capture dense object contact and force magnitude and used them to record a dataset of interactions from eight participants across diverse touch and grasp types. Our results demonstrate that EgoPHI recovers meaningful 3D contact and force distributions in simulated, out-of-distribution, and real-world settings, advancing egocentric hand-object understanding from contact localization toward physically grounded interaction reasoning.

AI.tldr: EgoPHI is the first method to jointly estimate dense contact maps and 3D force distributions on hand and object meshes from a single egocentric RGB image, using a physics-based simulation pipeline for training supervision and demonstrating strong performance on simulated, out-of-distribution, and real-world benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Understanding hand-object interaction from egocentric vision is essential, but existing methods only localize contact rather than estimating the physical forces acting on hands and objects, which is required for physically grounded interaction reasoning.
AI.method: EgoPHI jointly estimates dense contact maps and 3D force distributions on hand and object meshes from a single monocular RGB image and object geometry. It introduces a physics-based simulation pipeline that augments existing hand-object datasets with dense per-vertex force supervision to overcome the lack of scalable ground-truth force annotations.
AI.result: EgoPHI improves force estimation over existing approaches on in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, generalizes to unseen datasets, and recovers meaningful 3D contact and force distributions in simulated, out-of-distribution, and real-world settings (validated with physical objects and eight participants).
AI.conclusion: EgoPHI advances egocentric hand-object understanding from contact localization toward physically grounded interaction reasoning, demonstrating that force estimation from egocentric vision is feasible and generalizable across simulation and real-world scenarios.

title: RGB-D Video Generation for Improving Human-to-Robot Object Handover Prediction
summary: Human-to-robot (H2R) object handover is a fundamental capability for human-robot collaboration, yet progress is hindered by the scarcity of large-scale, human-centric datasets and the significant sim-to-real gap. To address these challenges, we introduce Hand2Bot, an RGB-D video dataset that provides rich contextual information such as body posture and facial expressions, specifically collected for handover scenarios with real-world noise patterns. We further propose PassGen, a generative pipeline that leverages stable video diffusion and an Intention-Aware Temporal Face Encoder to synthesize realistic handover sequences while ensuring hand-object consistency. To bridge the sim-to-real gap, we implement a morphology-based depth editing strategy that replicates realistic sensor noise found in physical depth maps. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our framework achieves high intention identification accuracy and low false trigger rates in both ablation studies and real-world deployment on a physical robot platform. Our results confirm that training on PassGen allows for robust zero-shot transfer and earlier intention anticipation compared to traditional hand-centric baselines, effectively enabling socially aware robotic behavior in shared workspaces.

AI.tldr: Hand2Bot is an RGB-D video dataset for human-to-robot object handover, paired with PassGen, a generative pipeline using stable video diffusion and an Intention-Aware Temporal Face Encoder to synthesize realistic handover sequences with morphology-based depth editing to bridge the sim-to-real gap. The framework achieves high intention identification accuracy, low false trigger rates, and robust zero-shot transfer in real-world robot deployment.
AI.motivation: Progress in human-to-robot object handover is limited by the lack of large-scale, human-centric datasets and the significant sim-to-real gap. Existing approaches fail to capture rich contextual cues like body posture and facial expressions that are essential for socially aware handover behavior.
AI.method: The authors introduce Hand2Bot, an RGB-D video dataset with real-world noise patterns containing body posture and facial expression context. They propose PassGen, a generative pipeline combining stable video diffusion with an Intention-Aware Temporal Face Encoder to synthesize handover sequences while maintaining hand-object consistency. A morphology-based depth editing strategy replicates realistic sensor noise to bridge sim-to-real gap.
AI.result: The framework achieves high intention identification accuracy and low false trigger rates in both ablation studies and real-world deployment on a physical robot platform. Training on PassGen enables robust zero-shot transfer and earlier intention anticipation compared to traditional hand-centric baselines.
AI.conclusion: PassGen-generated training data enables robust zero-shot transfer and earlier intention anticipation, effectively enabling socially aware robotic behavior in shared workspaces, confirming that human-centric contextual information is valuable for H2R handover tasks.

title: UniTraffic-Agent: Unified Traffic Video Reasoning for AI City Challenge 2026 Track 3 with Two Out-of-Domain Evaluations
comment: This paper has been accepted to ECCV 2026 AI City Challenge Workshop
summary: Traffic video understanding has become an important problem in intelligent transportation, as road videos provide direct evidence for accidents, violations, and interactions between vehicles and vulnerable road users. A useful system should explain how a traffic event develops, why it happens, and when the relevant interaction occurs, yet this remains difficult for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) because traffic videos contain sparse events and varied viewpoints. We introduce UniTraffic-Agent, the MR-CAS solution for Track~3 of the 10th AI City Challenge, which includes Traffic Anomaly Reasoning (TAR) and two out-of-domain evaluations: FETV for fisheye traffic events and PSI-VQA for pedestrian intention reasoning. UniTraffic-Agent follows an observe--reason--act--verify workflow that samples timestamped visual evidence, reasons over all questions from the same clip in one request, and converts responses through task-specific action adapters. On the official Public leaderboards, MR-CAS ranks 16th on TAR with a score of 0.5780, 2nd on FETV with 0.4884, and 4th on PSI-VQA with 64.4161. The code is available at https://github.com/Roclp/UniTraffic-Agent.

AI.tldr: UniTraffic-Agent is an MR-CAS solution for Track 3 of the 10th AI City Challenge that addresses traffic video understanding tasks including Traffic Anomaly Reasoning (TAR), fisheye traffic events (FETV), and pedestrian intention reasoning (PSI-VQA). It uses an observe-reason-act-verify workflow with timestamped visual evidence sampling and task-specific action adapters, achieving 16th on TAR (0.5780), 2nd on FETV (0.4884), and 4th on PSI-VQA (64.4161).
AI.motivation: Traffic video understanding is critical for intelligent transportation as it provides evidence for accidents, violations, and vehicle-vulnerable road user interactions. Existing multimodal large language models struggle with traffic videos because they contain sparse events and varied viewpoints, making it difficult to explain how traffic events develop, why they happen, and when relevant interactions occur.
AI.method: UniTraffic-Agent employs an observe-reason-act-verify workflow that: (1) samples timestamped visual evidence from videos, (2) reasons over all questions from the same clip in a single request to maintain context, and (3) converts responses through task-specific action adapters for each downstream task.
AI.result: On official Public leaderboards, MR-CAS ranks 16th on TAR with score 0.5780, 2nd on FETV with 0.4884, and 4th on PSI-VQA with 64.4161.
AI.conclusion: The proposed workflow effectively handles diverse traffic video understanding tasks across different viewpoints (standard, fisheye) and reasoning types (anomaly reasoning and pedestrian intention), with competitive performance demonstrated on the AI City Challenge leaderboards.

title: Spatially-Grounded Text-to-Video Generation via Inference-Time Gradient-Free Optimization
summary: Diffusion Transformer Text-to-Video models have achieved remarkable synthesis quality, yet fine-grained spatial controllability remains a significant challenge. While existing training-free methods produce solid overall results in spatially grounded generation, \ie, placing a specific object in a designated location, they rely on gradient-based optimization techniques that incur prohibitive computational overhead, a bottleneck amplified in modern large-scale architectures. To address this limitation, we present Gradient-free Analytical Trajectory Optimization Video Generation (GATO-Vid), a novel training-free and gradient-free approach for precise spatial guidance. Rather than relying on costly backward passes, we introduce an alternative cross-attention score and solve it analytically to obtain an exact, closed-form solution. To use our analytical solution, we propose an on-the-fly injection mechanism tailored to the topological manifold of the transformer's latent space. Our experiments demonstrate that GATO-Vid significantly outperforms existing baselines in localization accuracy while introducing minimal computational overhead.

AI.tldr: GATO-Vid is a training-free and gradient-free approach for fine-grained spatial control in Diffusion Transformer Text-to-Video models, using an analytical closed-form solution for cross-attention scores instead of costly gradient-based optimization, achieving better localization accuracy with minimal computational overhead.
AI.motivation: Existing training-free spatial control methods in Diffusion Transformer Text-to-Video models rely on gradient-based optimization, which incurs prohibitive computational overhead—a bottleneck that is amplified in modern large-scale architectures.
AI.method: GATO-Vid introduces an alternative cross-attention score solved analytically to obtain an exact, closed-form solution, avoid costly backward passes. It employs an on-the-fly injection mechanism tailored to the topological manifold of the transformer's latent space.
AI.result: GATO-Vid significantly outperforms existing baselines in localization accuracy while introducing minimal computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: Training-free and gradient-free spatial guidance is both feasible and superior in efficiency for diffusion transformer-based video generation, addressing the scalability bottleneck of gradient-based methods.

title: P2Fusion: Prompt-based Progressive Infrared-Visible Image Fusion via Dual-Prior Distillation
summary: Infrared-visible image fusion (IVIF) is pivotal for multimodal perception, yet reconciling the inherent information disparity between thermal and textural features remains a fundamental challenge. Existing prior-guided methods often rely on static constraints that induce optimization conflicts or utilize extrinsic semantic priors from large-scale foundation models (e.g., CLIP/DINO), which frequently fail to exploit the intrinsic modality characteristics essential for high-fidelity fusion. To address these issues, we propose P2Fusion, a prior-guided distillation-based framework that reformulates IVIF via dual intrinsic prompts. Instead of imposing hard-coded penalties, we distill image-intrinsic priors, thermal saliency and spatial quality, into learnable dynamic regulators. Specifically, a Teach-to-Fuse mechanism provides dual-granularity progressive guidance, coupled with a Gated Dynamic Expert Recalibration (GDER) module for decoupled feature refinement. This design enables the network to adaptively mediate modal competition through expert specialization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that P2Fusion achieves state-of-the-art performance across five mainstream datasets. Notably, our framework demonstrates consistent performance advantages in fusion quality, achieving state-of-the-art results in 14 out of 20 key evaluation metrics across 5 benchmarks. Furthermore, it effectively contributes to the robustness of downstream perception, such as +3.2% mAP on MSRS, +0.5% mAP on M3FD and +0.9% mAP on DroneVehicle for object detection. Our code will be available at https://github.com/YiShi99/P2Fusion

AI.tldr: P2Fusion is a prior-guided distillation framework for infrared-visible image fusion that uses dual intrinsic prompts (thermal saliency and spatial quality) with a Teach-to-Fuse mechanism and Gated Dynamic Expert Recalibration module to achieve state-of-the-art fusion quality across five datasets and improve downstream object detection performance.
AI.motivation: Existing prior-guided IVIF methods rely on static constraints causing optimization conflicts or external semantic priors from foundation models that fail to exploit intrinsic modality characteristics. The fundamental challenge is reconciling the information disparity between thermal and textural features in infrared-visible image fusion.
AI.method: P2Fusion reformulates IVIF through dual intrinsic prompts (thermal saliency and spatial quality) distilled into learnable dynamic regulators. It employs a Teach-to-Fuse mechanism for dual-granularity progressive guidance and a Gated Dynamic Expert Recalibration (GDER) module for decoupled feature refinement, enabling adaptive mediation of modal competition through expert specialization.
AI.result: P2Fusion achieves state-of-the-art performance on five mainstream datasets, with consistent advantages in fusion quality (SOTA in 14 of 20 key evaluation metrics). It also improves downstream object detection robustness: +3.2% mAP on MSRS, +0.5% mAP on M3FD, and +0.9% mAP on DroneVehicle.
AI.conclusion: P2Fusion demonstrates that distilling image-intrinsic priors into learnable regulators with expert specialization effectively addresses modality competition in IVIF, yielding superior fusion quality and downstream perception robustness compared to existing prior-guided approaches.

title: Topology-Unified 2D Pose Estimation across Intact, Residual and Prosthetic Limbs
summary: Driven by the availability of large-scale datasets, Human Pose Estimation (HPE) plays a critical role in numerous downstream tasks. However, mainstream benchmarks exhibit severe representation bias, predominantly featuring able-bodied individuals. While a few pioneering datasets have attempted to address limb differences, their annotation protocols fail to generalize, struggling to represent specialized mechanical structures like running blades or unprosthetized residual limbs. To bridge this gap, we introduce ProPose, a large-scale benchmark featuring a novel annotation protocol that unifies the topological representation of biological limbs, diverse prostheses, and physical absences within a single framework. Because real-world prosthetic images are inherently scarce and exhibit extreme long-tail distributions, we design a Real-to-Synthetic data expansion pipeline to explicitly synthesize and expand the underrepresented cases. However, simply training existing models on this enriched dataset often leads to suboptimal solutions, as they estimate each keypoint independently and might hallucinate non-existent joints on mechanical structures. To resolve this, we propose ProLoss, a structure-aware objective that enforces keypoint dependencies within a single limb to prevent unrealistic limb predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach improves the classification accuracy of long-tail prosthetic joints by 2% to 6% without compromising spatial coordinate localization performance. This work sets a foundation for inclusive pose estimation, unlocking new possibilities for understanding the interactions between human bodies and assistive devices.

AI.tldr: ProPose is a large-scale benchmark with a novel annotation protocol that unifies biological limbs, prostheses, and physical absences in a single topological framework, combined with a Real-to-Synthetic data expansion pipeline and a structure-aware ProLoss objective to improve inclusive human pose estimation for prosthetic users.
AI.motivation: Mainstream HPE benchmarks exhibit severe representation bias, predominantly featuring able-bodied individuals. Existing datasets addressing limb differences fail to generalize due to annotation protocols that cannot represent specialized mechanical structures like running blades or unprosthetized residual limbs.
AI.method: (1) Introduces ProPose, a large-scale benchmark with a novel annotation protocol unifying biological limbs, prostheses, and physical absences in one framework. (2) Designs a Real-to-Synthetic data expansion pipeline to synthesize and expand underrepresented prosthetic cases. (3) Proposes ProLoss, a structure-aware objective that enforces keypoint dependencies within a single limb to prevent hallucinating non-existent joints on mechanical structures.
AI.result: The approach improves classification accuracy of long-tail prosthetic joints by 2% to 6% without compromising spatial coordinate localization performance.
AI.conclusion: This work sets a foundation for inclusive pose estimation, unlocking new possibilities for understanding interactions between human bodies and assistive devices.

title: Learning Unified Video and Image Representation for Video Face Forgery Detection
summary: Face forgery detection is crucial for preserving the security and integrity of facial data given the rapid developments in face manipulation techniques and deep generative models. Existing methods for video face forgery detection typically assume that all frames in a forged video are manipulated, while detecting partially forged videos that contain only a subset of altered frames remains challenging. To address this issue, we propose a novel framework, UVIF, that utilizes additional annotated images to provide fine-grained supervision for detecting partial forgeries in videos. UVIF employs a unified encoder and a multi-task learning paradigm to jointly model facial videos and images for boosted video face forgery detection. A 2D backbone with temporal fusion modules is employed as the unified encoder. A pseudo labeling process is designed for video frames to bridge their representations with those of static images. A video-oriented feature alignment strategy is further introduced to reduce the distribution gap between videos and images. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework, which outperforms state-of-theart methods in detecting partially forged videos while introducing no additional computational overhead. Our code is available at https://github.com/haotianll/UVIF.

AI.tldr: UVIF is a novel framework for detecting partially forged videos in face forgery detection, using annotated images to provide fine-grained supervision through a unified encoder and multi-task learning paradigm, achieving state-of-the-art performance without additional computational overhead.
AI.motivation: Existing video face forgery detection methods assume all frames in a forged video are manipulated, but real-world forged videos often contain only a subset of altered frames. Detecting these partially forged videos remains a critical and unsolved challenge.
AI.method: UVIF uses a unified encoder (2D backbone with temporal fusion modules) and a multi-task learning paradigm to jointly model facial videos and images. It employs a pseudo labeling process for video frames to bridge representations with static images, and a video-oriented feature alignment strategy to reduce the distribution gap between videos and images.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show UVIF outperforms state-of-the-art methods in detecting partially forged videos while introducing no additional computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging additional annotated images with fine-grained supervision via a unified multi-task framework effectively improves partial forgery detection in videos, and the code is publicly available.

title: Paths: Prompt-aware Spatio-temporal Transformer with Hierarchical Multi-modal Fusion for RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification
comment: Accepted by ACM MM2026. More modifications may be performed
summary: RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification (RE-VReID) aims to retrieve specific person across non-overlapping cameras with complementary RGB videos and event streams. However, existing methods often decouple spatial and temporal modeling, which limits their interaction. In addition, global-level RGB-Event fusion fails to fully exploit fine-grained discriminative cues. To address these issues, we propose Paths, a unified framework with spatio-temporal modeling and hierarchical multi-modal fusion for RE-VReID. Specifically, we first design a Memory-Augmented Backbone (MAB) to maintain modality-specific identity prototypes for stable intra-modal representation learning. Then, we propose a Prompt-aware Spatio-temporal Transformer (PST) to jointly model spatial and temporal cues within a unified Transformer. Finally, we introduce a Hierarchical Multi-modal Fusion (HMF) to integrate RGB and event features at global and local levels. With these modules, our framework can learn robust and discriminative representations for RE-VReID. Extensive experiments on three public RE-VReID benchmarks including EvReID, MARS and iLIDS-VID, demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. The code is available at https://github.com/Reflection0427/Paths.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Paths, a unified framework for RGB-Event Video Person Re-Identification that jointly models spatio-temporal cues via a Prompt-aware Spatio-temporal Transformer, maintains modality-specific identity prototypes with a Memory-Augmented Backbone, and integrates RGB-event features hierarchically at global and local levels. Extensive experiments on EvReID, MARS, and iLIDS-VID benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness.
AI.motivation: Existing RE-VReID methods decouple spatial and temporal modeling, limiting their interaction, and global-level RGB-Event fusion fails to exploit fine-grained discriminative cues.
AI.method: The framework consists of three key modules: (1) Memory-Augmented Backbone (MAB) maintains modality-specific identity prototypes for stable intra-modal representation learning; (2) Prompt-aware Spatio-temporal Transformer (PST) jointly models spatial and temporal cues within a unified Transformer; (3) Hierarchical Multi-modal Fusion (HMF) integrates RGB and event features at both global and local levels.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three public RE-VReID benchmarks (EvReID, MARS, iLIDS-VID) demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Paths framework can learn robust and discriminative representations for RE-VReID by jointly modeling spatio-temporal information and performing hierarchical multi-modal fusion.

title: RbFT-Net: Rectify-Before-Fuse Temporal Radar Anchors for 4D Radar-Camera Depth Completion
summary: Dense metric depth prediction from cameras and millimeter-wave radar offers a cost-effective sensing solution for autonomous systems. However, radar measurements are inherently sparse and susceptible to clutter, multipath reflections, and projection errors. While aggregating multiple radar frames provides denser metric cues, it also introduces temporal misalignment and dynamic-object interference. Directly propagating such unreliable measurements can therefore corrupt large regions of the predicted depth map. To address this issue, we propose RbFT-Net, an end-to-end rectify-before-fuse framework for multi-frame 4D radar-camera depth completion. Rather than assuming accumulated radar returns to be accurate, RbFT-Net treats them as noisy temporal anchor candidates. An image-conditioned rectification module jointly corrects their image-plane locations and metric depths while estimating pointwise reliability. The rectified anchors are then selectively propagated before high-level multi-modal fusion, suppressing the influence of unreliable measurements. Experiments on ZJU-4DRadarCam and a newly collected 4D radar-camera-LiDAR dataset show that RbFT-Net consistently outperforms the evaluated independent radar-camera methods and remains competitive with plug-in pipelines using auxiliary monocular depth models. Cross-platform evaluation and component analyses further support the effectiveness of the proposed rectification and reliability-aware propagation strategy.

AI.tldr: RbFT-Net is an end-to-end rectify-before-fuse framework for multi-frame 4D radar-camera depth completion that treats accumulated radar returns as noisy temporal anchor candidates, corrects them via an image-conditioned rectification module, and selectively propagates rectified anchors before high-level multi-modal fusion to suppress unreliable measurements.
AI.motivation: Radar measurements are inherently sparse and susceptible to clutter, multipath reflections, and projection errors. Aggregating multiple radar frames provides denser cues but introduces temporal misalignment and dynamic-object interference, and directly propagating such unreliable measurements can corrupt large regions of the predicted depth map. The paper argues that conventional approaches assume accumulated radar returns to be accurate, which is problematic.
AI.method: RbFT-Net is an end-to-end rectify-before-fuse framework. It treats accumulated radar returns as noisy temporal anchor candidates rather than accurate measurements. An image-conditioned rectification module jointly corrects image-plane locations and metric depths while estimating pointwise reliability. The rectified anchors are selectively propagated before high-level multi-modal fusion, suppressing unreliable measurements' influence.
AI.result: Experiments on ZJU-4DRadarCam and a newly collected 4D radar-camera-LiDAR dataset show RbFT-Net consistently outperforms evaluated independent radar-camera methods and remains competitive with plug-in pipelines using auxiliary monocular depth models. Cross-platform evaluation and component analyses support the effectiveness of the rectification and reliability-aware propagation strategy.
AI.conclusion: The rectify-before-fuse paradigm is an effective approach for multi-frame 4D radar-camera depth completion, addressing the reliability issues of accumulated radar measurements and improving depth prediction quality.

title: Online Learning of Correspondences between Images
summary: We propose a novel method for iterative learning of point correspondences between image sequences. Points moving on surfaces in 3D space are projected into two images. Given a point in either view, the considered problem is to determine the corresponding location in the other view. The geometry and distortions of the projections are unknown as is the shape of the surface. Given several pairs of point-sets but no access to the 3D scene, correspondence mappings can be found by excessive global optimization or by the fundamental matrix if a perspective projective model is assumed. However, an iterative solution on sequences of point-set pairs with general imaging geometry is preferable. We derive such a method that optimizes the mapping based on Neyman's chi-square divergence between the densities representing the uncertainties of the estimated and the actual locations. The densities are represented as channel vectors computed with a basis function approach. The mapping between these vectors is updated with each new pair of images such that fast convergence and high accuracy are achieved. The resulting algorithm runs in real-time and is superior to state-of-the-art methods in terms of convergence and accuracy in a number of experiments.

AI.tldr: A novel iterative method for learning point correspondences between image sequences using Neyman's chi-square divergence between channel-vector density representations, achieving real-time performance and superior accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Correspondence mapping between image sequences is challenging when geometry, projection distortions, and surface shape are unknown. Existing solutions rely on excessive global optimization or assume a perspective projective model via the fundamental matrix. An iterative solution that handles general imaging geometry is needed.
AI.method: The method optimizes the correspondence mapping based on Neyman's chi-square divergence between probability densities representing uncertainties of estimated and actual point locations. Densities are represented as channel vectors using a basis function approach, and the mapping between these vectors is iteratively updated with each new image pair for fast convergence.
AI.result: The algorithm runs in real-time and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of convergence speed and accuracy across a number of experiments.
