AI.conclusion: The proposed iterative learning approach provides an efficient and accurate solution for point correspondence in image sequences under general imaging geometry, surpassing existing methods without requiring global optimization or restrictive projection models.

title: Towards Physics-Faithful Generation of Scientific Diagrams
summary: Text-to-image generation has reached photorealistic quality, yet state-of-the-art systems remain unreliable at producing scientific diagrams, whose value depends not on appearance but on physical faithfulness: correct force directions, valid coordinate systems, consistent thermodynamic states, and equations matching the depicted scenario. Trained on web imagery with physically shallow captions, generic models produce diagrams that look plausible but are physically wrong, harmful in education and scientific communication. We present Princigram, a physics-faithful scientific-diagram generator, and its data pipeline. Our central advance is Structured Physical Chain-of-Thought (SP-CoT): a per-subdiscipline schema that decomposes a physics diagram into an explicit multi-step reasoning chain across six subdisciplines, from scene identification through force or process analysis to governing laws and synthesis. Unlike free-form chain-of-thought, SP-CoT follows a fixed schema with strict fidelity rules that separate visually grounded facts from physically inferred reasoning and type all mathematics symbolically; it serves both as dense training supervision and, at inference, as a structured "thinking" prompt. With it we curate and structurally annotate 4.3 million physics images, of which 115,037 carry expert-level annotation, and adapt a unified multimodal backbone. We further introduce VeriphyT2IBench, whose questions are derived from each held-out diagram's own structured annotation: each diagram becomes an item-specific bank of binary questions about its objects, forces, and states, so a judge model's score decomposes into named physical facts rather than one holistic number. On the physics subset of GenExam and on VeriphyT2IBench, Princigram shows that explicit physics-structured supervision improves the physical faithfulness of generated scientific diagrams.

AI.tldr: Princigram is a physics-faithful scientific-diagram generator using Structured Physical Chain-of-Thought (SP-CoT), a per-subdiscipline schema decomposing diagram reasoning into explicit multi-step chains. It curates 4.3M physics images (115K expert-annotated), adapts a unified multimodal backbone, and introduces VeriphyT2IBench for item-specific physical-fact evaluation. Results show structured physics supervision improves diagram physical faithfulness.
AI.motivation: State-of-the-art text-to-image systems can generate photorealistic images but fail to produce physically correct scientific diagrams, which require physical faithfulness (correct forces, coordinates, thermodynamic states, matching equations) rather than visual plausibility. Generic models trained on web imagery with shallow captions produce diagrams that look plausible but are physically wrong, which is harmful in education and scientific communication.
AI.method: Introduces Structured Physical Chain-of-Thought (SP-CoT): a per-subdiscipline schema decomposing physics diagrams into explicit multi-step reasoning chains across six subdisciplines, from scene identification through force/process analysis to governing laws and synthesis. SP-CoT uses a fixed schema with strict fidelity rules separating visually grounded facts from physically inferred reasoning, with symbolic math typing. Serves as dense training supervision and structured "thinking" prompt at inference. Curates and structurally annotates 4.3M physics images (115,037 expert-annotated) and adapts a unified multimodal backbone. Also introduces VeriphyT2IBench for item-specific binary-question evaluation.
AI.result: On the physics subset of GenExam and on VeriphyT2IBench, Princigram demonstrates that explicit physics-structured supervision improves the physical faithfulness of generated scientific diagrams compared to generic models.
AI.conclusion: Explicit physics-structured supervision via SP-CoT and structured annotations improves physical faithfulness in scientific diagram generation, addressing the gap where generic models produce visually plausible but physically incorrect diagrams.

title: EgoMonth: A Month-Level Egocentric Video Benchmark for Long-Term Spatiotemporal Memory
summary: Recent advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have led to substantial progress in video understanding, accompanied by a growing number of long video benchmarks. However, existing benchmarks rely predominantly on web-sourced videos that lack inter-clip spatiotemporal continuity, making it difficult to assess whether models can maintain consistent memory across days or weeks of real-world experience. We introduce EgoMonth, the first month-level egocentric video understanding benchmark. EgoMonth comprises over 300 hours of first-person daily-life recordings from 20 participants spanning 20 to 120 days, paired with 1,443 human-crafted multiple-choice question-answer pairs. We design a cognitively grounded 14-task evaluation framework organized into three hierarchical cognitive levels: Schema Consolidation, Episodic Indexing, and Cascading Reasoning. Evaluation of state-of-the-art open-source and closed-source MLLMs reveals that even the best-performing model, Gemini 2.5 Pro, achieves only 71.8% macro-average accuracy, remaining 22.4 percentage points below the corrected human baseline of 94.2%. Several models perform near or below the 25% chance level on tasks such as Route Reasoning, Cross-view Spatial Reasoning, and Direction Judgement, while even the strongest closed-source model remains substantially below human performance. These results indicate that current MLLMs function as lossy summarizers rather than faithful memorizers, highlighting the need for architectures with genuine long-term spatiotemporal memory.

AI.tldr: EgoMonth is the first month-level egocentric video understanding benchmark, comprising over 300 hours of first-person recordings from 20 participants spanning 20-120 days with 1,443 human-crafted QA pairs across a 14-task, three-level cognitive evaluation framework. State-of-the-art MLLMs achieve at most 71.8% accuracy (Gemini 2.5 Pro), far below the 94.2% human baseline, with several models near chance level on spatial reasoning tasks, revealing that current MLLMs are lossy summarizers without genuine long-term spatiotemporal memory.
AI.motivation: Existing long video benchmarks rely on web-sourced videos lacking inter-clip spatiotemporal continuity, so they cannot assess whether MLLMs maintain consistent memory across days or weeks of real-world experience. A month-level egocentric benchmark is needed to evaluate genuine long-term memory in MLLMs.
AI.method: The authors construct EgoMonth with 300+ hours of first-person daily-life recordings from 20 participants over 20-120 days, paired with 1,443 human-crafted multiple-choice QA pairs. They design a cognitively grounded 14-task evaluation framework organized into three hierarchical cognitive levels: Schema Consolidation, Episodic Indexing, and Cascading Reasoning.
AI.result: Gemini 2.5 Pro achieves the best macro-average accuracy of 71.8%, still 22.4 points below the corrected human baseline of 94.2%. Several models perform near or below 25% chance level on Route Reasoning, Cross-view Spatial Reasoning, and Direction Judgement tasks.
AI.conclusion: Current MLLMs function as lossy summarizers rather than faithful memorizers, highlighting the need for architectures with genuine long-term spatiotemporal memory to handle real-world egocentric video understanding at month-level temporal scales.

title: Fast Iterative Five point Relative Pose Estimation
summary: Robust estimation of the relative pose between two cameras is a fundamental part of Structure and Motion methods. For calibrated cameras, the five point method together with a robust estimator such as RANSAC gives the best result in most cases. The current state-of-the-art method for solving the relative pose problem from five points is due to Nister [9], because it is faster than other methods and in the RANSAC scheme one can improve precision by increasing the number of iterations. In this paper, we propose a new iterative method, which is based on Powell's Dog Leg algorithm. The new method has the same precision and is approximately twice as fast as Nister's algorithm. The proposed method is easily extended to more than five points while retaining a efficient error metrics. This makes it also very suitable as an refinement step. The proposed algorithm is systematically evaluated on three types of datasets with known ground truth.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a new iterative method for robust relative pose estimation between two cameras, based on Powell's Dog Leg algorithm. It matches Nister's five-point method in precision while being approximately twice as fast, extends naturally to more than five points, and serves as an effective refinement step.
AI.motivation: The five-point method by Nister is the current state-of-the-art for relative pose estimation, but it is computationally expensive. In RANSAC schemes, more iterations can improve precision, so a faster algorithm provides a significant advantage. There is a need for a faster method with equivalent precision.
AI.method: The authors propose an iterative method based on Powell's Dog Leg algorithm for solving the relative pose problem from five points. The method achieves the same precision as Nister's algorithm while being approximately twice as fast. It is also designed to be easily extended to more than five points with efficient error metrics, making it suitable as a refinement step.
AI.result: The proposed algorithm is systematically evaluated on three types of datasets with known ground truth. It demonstrates the same precision as Nister's method while being approximately twice as fast.
AI.conclusion: The Dog Leg-based iterative method offers a faster alternative to Nister's five-point algorithm with equivalent precision, and its extensibility to multiple points makes it valuable both for hypothesis generation in RANSAC and as a refinement step in Structure and Motion pipelines.

title: QuISE: Defense against Typographic Attacks on VLMs via Query-Irrelevant Semantic Editing
summary: Typographic attacks pose a critical threat to vision-language models (VLMs) by injecting misleading text into images and causing models to rely on adversarial textual cues rather than visual evidence. Existing defenses often require model-specific modifications, additional training, or access to internal model components, limiting their applicability to modern closed-source VLMs. In this paper, we propose QuISE, a model-agnostic, training-free black-box defense based on query-irrelevant semantic editing. QuISE first identifies text regions likely to affect the current query through influence-aware text localization. QuISE then replaces these regions with two semantically distinct replacement texts that are irrelevant to both the query and the image. The final answer is determined by answer consistency across the edited images. Extensive experiments on three typographic-attack benchmarks, four attack settings, and four VLMs show that QuISE consistently improves defended accuracy. QuISE achieves a recovery rate of 67.9-75.0% with a harm rate of 0.5-1.1%.

AI.tldr: QuISE is a model-agnostic, training-free black-box defense against typographic attacks on VLMs. It identifies query-influential text regions in images, replaces them with semantically irrelevant text, and determines answers via consistency across edited images. It achieves 67.9-75.0% recovery rate with only 0.5-1.1% harm rate across multiple benchmarks and VLMs.
AI.motivation: Typographic attacks trick VLMs into relying on adversarial text in images rather than visual evidence. Existing defenses require model-specific modifications, additional training, or internal model access, making them unsuitable for modern closed-source VLMs. A black-box, model-agnostic defense is needed.
AI.method: QuISE (query-irrelevant semantic editing) operates in two stages: (1) influence-aware text localization to identify text regions most likely to affect the current query, and (2) replacing those regions with two semantically distinct texts that are irrelevant to both the query and the image. The final prediction is determined by answer consistency across the edited image variants.
AI.result: On three typographic-attack benchmarks, four attack settings, and four VLMs, QuISE consistently improves defended accuracy, achieving a recovery rate of 67.9-75.0% with a harm rate of only 0.5-1.1%.
AI.conclusion: QuISE provides an effective, practical defense against typographic attacks that works without model modification, training, or internal access, making it applicable to closed-source commercial VLMs while minimizing harm to benign inputs.

title: Predicting Signed Distance Functions for Visual Instance Segmentation
summary: Visual instance segmentation is a challenging problem and becomes even more difficult if objects of interest varies unconstrained in shape. Some objects are well described by a rectangle, however, this is hardly always the case. Consider for instance long, slender objects such as ropes. Anchor-based approaches classify predefined bounding boxes as either negative or positive and thus provide a limited set of shapes that can be handled. Defining anchor-boxes that fit well to all possible shapes leads to an infeasible number of prior boxes. We explore a different approach and propose to train a neural network to compute distance maps along different directions. The network is trained at each pixel to predict the distance to the closest object contour in a given direction. By pooling the distance maps we obtain an approximation to the signed distance function (SDF). The SDF may then be thresholded in order to obtain a foreground-background segmentation. We compare this segmentation to foreground segmentations obtained from the state-of-the-art instance segmentation method YOLACT. On the COCO dataset, our segmentation yields a higher performance in terms of foreground intersection over union (IoU). However, while the distance maps contain information on the individual instances, it is not straightforward to map them to the full instance segmentation. We still believe that this idea is a promising research direction for instance segmentation, as it better captures the different shapes found in the real world.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a novel approach to visual instance segmentation by training a neural network to predict distance maps from each pixel to the closest object contour in various directions. These distance maps are pooled to approximate the signed distance function (SDF), which is then thresholded to obtain foreground-background segmentation. This approach outperforms YOLACT on foreground IoU for COCO, but mapping distance maps to full instance segmentation remains challenging.
AI.motivation: Traditional anchor-based instance segmentation methods rely on predefined bounding boxes, which poorly handle objects with unconstrained shapes such as long, slender objects (e.g., ropes). Defining anchors that fit all possible shapes requires an infeasible number of prior boxes, motivating an alternative approach.
AI.method: A neural network is trained per-pixel to predict distance maps to the closest object contour in different directions. These directional distance maps are pooled to approximate the signed distance function (SDF), which is then thresholded to produce a foreground-background segmentation.
AI.result: On the COCO dataset, the proposed segmentation method achieves higher foreground intersection over union (IoU) compared to the state-of-the-art instance segmentation method YOLACT.
AI.conclusion: While the method shows promising segmentation quality and better captures diverse real-world shapes, mapping the distance maps to full instance segmentation remains non-trivial. The authors believe this direction holds promise for improving instance segmentation of arbitrarily shaped objects.

title: MergeOver: Post-Training Token Merging for Recursive Vision Transformers
summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) demonstrate exceptional performance in computer vision but suffer from large parameter counts and quadratic computational complexity, severely limiting their deployment on resource-constrained edge hardware. While recursive weight-sharing reduces parameter counts and token merging mitigates computational and memory bottlenecks, integrating these two paradigms without costly retraining is non-trivial, leaving this intersection largely unexplored. We propose MergeOver, a post-training approach that integrates Token Merging (ToMe) into the recursively weight-shared Sliced Recursive Transformer (SReT). Through an Unmerge tracking stack, constraint-safe merge-rate adjustment, and synchronised token-mass tracking across spatial permutations, MergeOver resolves the spatial and merging constraints of this integration. We further employ a stage-wise single-shot schedule that performs token reduction at the first block of each stage and maintains a fixed sequence length throughout its subsequent recursive iterations. Benchmarked on ImageNet-1K, our selected configuration reduces top-1 accuracy by 1.47 percentage points. On the GPU, it reduces peak activation memory by 37.3% and 38.4% at batch sizes 1 and 16, while throughput decreases by 21.7% at batch size 1 but increases by 21.7% at batch size 16. On a Raspberry Pi 5 (ARM CPU), it reduces latency by 2.4% and 17.6% at batch sizes 1 and 16. These results show that MergeOver can recover a meaningful part of the throughput and memory cost that recursive weight-sharing introduces, without retraining, and provides a baseline for combining token merging with hierarchical recursive transformers.

AI.tldr: MergeOver is a post-training approach that integrates Token Merging (ToMe) into the recursively weight-shared Sliced Recursive Transformer (SReT), resolving spatial and merging constraints through an Unmerge tracking stack and constraint-safe merge-rate adjustment, achieving meaningful memory and latency reductions without retraining.
AI.motivation: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have large parameter counts and quadratic computational complexity, limiting edge deployment. While recursive weight-sharing reduces parameters and token merging mitigates computation/memory bottlenecks, integrating these two paradigms without retraining is non-trivial and largely unexplored.
AI.method: MergeOver is a post-training method that integrates ToMe into SReT. It uses an Unmerge tracking stack, constraint-safe merge-rate adjustment, and synchronized token-mass tracking across spatial permutations. It employs a stage-wise single-shot schedule that performs token reduction at the first block of each stage, maintaining a fixed sequence length through subsequent recursive iterations.
AI.result: On ImageNet-1K, top-1 accuracy drops by 1.47 percentage points. Peak activation memory is reduced by 37.3% and 38.4% at batch sizes 1 and 16 on GPU. Throughput decreases by 21.7% at batch size 1 but increases by 21.7% at batch size 16. On Raspberry Pi 5 (ARM CPU), latency is reduced by 2.4% and 17.6% at batch sizes 1 and 16.
AI.conclusion: MergeOver recovers a meaningful portion of the throughput and memory cost introduced by recursive weight-sharing without retraining, providing a baseline for combining token merging with hierarchical recursive transformers.

title: Geometry-Grounded Unified 3D Perception for Autonomous Driving
summary: Camera-based autonomous driving perception requires a shared representation that preserves metric 3D structure across synchronized multi-camera streams. However, existing image-based frameworks often rely on backbones pretrained for semantic recognition, and introduce 3D geometry through downstream task-specific modules. As a result, their shared representations may fail to preserve explicit metric geometry and consistent 3D scene structure. In this paper, we present a Geometry-grounded Unified 3D Perception (GeoUP) framework that adapts the reconstruction-oriented latent of VGGT to calibrated, streaming multi-camera driving scenes. GeoUP factorizes cross-image interaction into self, temporal, and view attention to capture structurally distinct temporal and cross-view correspondences. It further injects calibration-aware raymap encodings to provide metric scale and camera geometry. The resulting geometry-grounded latent is decoded for metric depth estimation, 3D object detection, and semantic occupancy prediction, corresponding to surface-, instance-, and volume-level readouts of the same 3D scene. Through joint multi-task and multi-dataset training, GeoUP effectively leverages heterogeneous annotations and generalizes across diverse sensor configurations and perception ranges. Extensive experiments on nuScenes, Argoverse 2, Waymo, KITTI, and DDAD demonstrate that GeoUP achieves SOTA performance across detection, occupancy, and depth estimation. These results validate the effectiveness of geometry-grounded representations for unified 3D driving perception.

AI.tldr: GeoUP is a framework that adapts the reconstruction-oriented latent of VGGT to multi-camera driving scenes, factorizing cross-image attention into self, temporal, and view streams with calibration-aware raymap encodings, enabling unified metric depth estimation, 3D object detection, and semantic occupancy prediction with SOTA results across five benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing image-based multi-camera driving perception frameworks rely on backbones pretrained for semantic recognition and introduce 3D geometry only through downstream task-specific modules, causing shared representations to fail in preserving explicit metric geometry and consistent 3D scene structure across synchronized camera streams.
AI.method: The paper presents GeoUP, which adapts VGGT's reconstruction-oriented latent to streaming multi-camera driving data. It factorizes cross-image interactions into self, temporal, and view attention for capturing distinct temporal and cross-view correspondences, and injects calibration-aware raymap encodings to provide metric scale and camera geometry. The geometry-grounded latent is decoded for three tasks (metric depth estimation, 3D object detection, semantic occupancy prediction) with joint multi-task and multi-dataset training.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on nuScenes, Argoverse 2, Waymo, KITTI, and DDAD show GeoUP achieves state-of-the-art performance across 3D detection, occupancy prediction, and depth estimation, demonstrating strong generalization across diverse sensor configurations and perception ranges.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-grounded representations are effective for unified 3D driving perception, validating the approach of anchoring shared representations in explicit metric geometry rather than semantic-only pretraining.

title: Less Annotation, More Interpretation: Prior-Guided Concept Bottleneck Models for Interpretable Cancer Imaging Diagnosis
comment: Accepted at the iMIMIC Workshop at MICCAI 2026
summary: Concept bottleneck models (CBMs) can improve the transparency of cancer image diagnostic prediction by expressing predictions through radiological concepts. However, their dependence on instance-level concept annotations limits practical applicability. We propose a prior-guided hybrid CBM that integrates limited concept annotations, class-conditional concept distribution matching on unannotated patients, and prior initialization of the concept-to-diagnosis head. We evaluate the method on CBIS-DDSM mammographic masses and calcifications and LIDC-IDRI pulmonary nodules across 0-100% concept annotation. In the clinically relevant 0-20% annotation regime, the hybrid CBM consistently improves mean concept AUC over a matched standard CBM, while maintaining diagnostic performance close to black-box models. At 10% annotation specifically, concept AUC increases from 0.619 to 0.741 for masses, from 0.650 to 0.787 for calcifications, and from 0.597 to 0.642 for pulmonary nodules. Ablation experiments identify prior initialization as the main component contributing to improved concept detection, likely by stabilizing the concept-to-diagnosis head. Zero-shot VLMs remain insufficient for reliable fine-grained tumor-level concept prediction. These findings suggest that structured priors can substantially reduce the annotation burden of interpretable cancer imaging models.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a prior-guided hybrid concept bottleneck model (CBM) that improves interpretable cancer imaging by integrating limited concept annotations, class-conditional concept distribution matching, and prior initialization of the concept-to-diagnosis head, demonstrating significant concept detection improvements at low annotation rates (0-20%) across mammographic and pulmonary nodule datasets.
AI.motivation: Concept bottleneck models enhance transparency in cancer diagnosis by expressing predictions through radiological concepts, but their reliance on instance-level concept annotations severely limits practical applicability due to the high annotation burden.
AI.method: The proposed prior-guided hybrid CBM combines three components: (1) limited concept annotations for labeled patients, (2) class-conditional concept distribution matching on unannotated patients to leverage unlabeled data, and (3) prior initialization of the concept-to-diagnosis head to stabilize training.
AI.result: At 10% annotation, concept AUC improved from 0.619 to 0.741 for masses, 0.650 to 0.787 for calcifications, and 0.597 to 0.642 for pulmonary nodules, while maintaining diagnostic performance close to black-box models. Ablations show prior initialization is the key contributing component, and zero-shot VLMs remain insufficient for fine-grained tumor-level concept prediction.
AI.conclusion: Structured priors can substantially reduce the annotation burden of interpretable cancer imaging models, making CBMs more practical for clinical applications in the low-annotation regime.

title: Splat-based Metal Artifact Reduction in Cone-Beam CT via Polychromatic Modeling
summary: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) enables volumetric reconstruction from X-ray projections, but suffers from severe artifacts--especially beam hardening--when imaging materials with high attenuation such as metals. These artifacts arise from the polychromatic nature of X-rays and are not properly addressed by conventional monochromatic reconstruction algorithms. While recent neural representation-based methods offer improved reconstruction quality, they are computationally expensive and often impractical for deployment. We propose a novel physics-inspired, self-calibrating metal artifact reduction method that efficiently reconstructs 3D CBCT volumes while correcting beam hardening artifacts. Our method integrates a polychromatic X-ray projection model, material-dependent attenuation profiles, and system response modeling into a Gaussian Splatting framework. Unlike prior work, we eliminate the need for manual metal masks or strong prior assumptions, and we optimize both reconstruction parameters and X-ray spectral characteristics jointly during training. We further introduce a high-fidelity synthetic CBCT dataset generation pipeline validated on Monte-Carlo x-ray simulation toolbox and release new datasets with severe metal-induced artifacts to support the community. This is the first splat-based method for reducing beam hardening in CBCT. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in artifact suppression and reconstruction accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a physics-inspired, self-calibrating metal artifact reduction method for cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) that integrates polychromatic X-ray projection modeling, material-dependent attenuation profiles, and system response into a Gaussian Splatting framework. It jointly optimizes reconstruction parameters and X-ray spectral characteristics without requiring manual metal masks, and introduces a high-fidelity synthetic CBCT dataset generation pipeline with severe metal-induced artifacts.
AI.motivation: CBCT suffers from severe artifacts (especially beam hardening) when imaging highly attenuating materials like metals, because conventional monochromatic reconstruction algorithms fail to account for the polychromatic nature of X-rays. Existing neural representation-based methods improve quality but are computationally expensive and impractical for real deployment.
AI.method: The method integrates a polychromatic X-ray projection model, material-dependent attenuation profiles, and system response modeling into a Gaussian Splatting framework. It jointly optimizes reconstruction parameters and X-ray spectral characteristics during training, eliminating the need for manual metal masks or strong prior assumptions. A high-fidelity synthetic CBCT dataset generation pipeline validated on Monte-Carlo x-ray simulation is also introduced.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in artifact suppression and reconstruction accuracy. It is the first splat-based method for reducing beam hardening in CBCT.
AI.conclusion: The proposed physics-inspired Gaussian Splatting approach successfully addresses beam hardening artifacts in CBCT in an efficient, self-calibrating manner, offering practical deployability while surpassing existing methods, and contributes new datasets to support further community research.

title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint
comment: 10 Pages excluding Reference and Appendix, Published at COLM 2026
summary: When visual evidence is occluded or chaotic, models should abstain. In this paper, we show that Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can internally distinguish when abstention is required, but fail to express it anyway. We introduce TRAPSBench, a procedurally generated video benchmark of 1,404 matched physics pairs in which a single targeted change renders the outcome undeterminable from the visual evidence. Furthermore, we introduce Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score (PECS), a new robust metric that requires models to both answer correctly when the outcome is knowable, and abstain when the outcome is not. Across 16 VLMs spanning five families, spontaneous restraint is poor: the best PECS is 0.292. The bottleneck is expression, not perception: linear probes decode answerability from hidden states at up to 0.91 AUROC across physics domains; steering a single-layer void direction causally induces or suppresses abstention. Our results replicate across three open-weight families (Qwen, Gemma, LLaVA). The failure is also more pronounced in visual than textual uncertainty: models detect textual impossibility about 4x more readily than missing visual evidence. Closing this representation--output gap likely requires output-stage interventions.

AI.tldr: VLMs internally know when to abstain from answering under visual uncertainty but fail to express this abstention. The authors introduce TRAPSBench (1,404 paired physics video tasks) and PECS metric, showing poor spontaneous restraint (best PECS 0.292) across 16 VLMs, despite hidden states decoding answerability at up to 0.91 AUROC—indicating a representation-output gap rather than a perception failure.
AI.motivation: Models should abstain when visual evidence is occluded or chaotic, but current VLMs fail to do so. The paper aims to determine whether this failure stems from perception (inability to detect uncertainty) or expression (inability to act on it).
AI.method: Introduces TRAPSBench, a procedurally generated video benchmark of 1,404 matched physics pairs with targeted changes making outcomes undeterminable; and PECS, a metric requiring correct answers when outcomes are knowable and abstention when they are not. Uses linear probes on hidden states and steering of a single-layer void direction to test causal intervention.
AI.result: Best PECS is 0.292 across 16 VLMs spanning five families. Linear probes decode answerability from hidden states at up to 0.91 AUROC. Steering a void direction causally induces or suppresses abstention. Results replicate across Qwen, Gemma, and LLaVA. Textual impossibility is detected ~4x more readily than missing visual evidence.
AI.conclusion: The failure to abstain is an expression bottleneck, not a perception problem. Closing this representation-output gap likely requires output-stage interventions rather than improved perception alone.

title: A Controlled Study of Self-Supervised Image and Video Pretraining under Limited Resources
summary: Visual foundation models are a cornerstone of image and video understanding but typically require large amounts of data and computation. The current scale required for pretraining visual foundation models may be unsustainable or unnecessary, and significant benefits arise when effective models can be obtained with fewer resources. To better understand how self-supervised learning (SSL) objectives behave under resource constraints, we conduct a controlled study of image and video SSL objectives under matched data, architecture, and compute budgets. We compare contrastive, reconstruction, feature-prediction, and diffusion objectives and evaluate both standalone and jointly trained image-video SSL formulations across a diverse set of image and video understanding tasks. Our results show that DINOv2-style pretraining consistently provides the strongest overall performance under limited resources. Furthermore, combining DINOv2 with video SSL objectives such as VideoMAE substantially improves image classification and segmentation performance, but degrades video tracking and camera-pose estimation performance, revealing an important tradeoff between semantic and geometric representation learning. These findings suggest that combining image and video SSL objectives can be beneficial in resource-limited settings, while highlighting the need for improved methods that better balance semantic, temporal, and geometric supervision.

AI.tldr: A controlled study comparing image and video self-supervised learning (SSL) objectives under matched data, architecture, and compute budgets, finding DINOv2-style pretraining performs best under limited resources, and that combining image and video SSL objectives improves semantic tasks but degrades geometric tasks.
AI.motivation: Visual foundation models typically require large amounts of data and computation, which may be unsustainable or unnecessary. The authors aim to understand how SSL objectives behave under resource constraints to identify more efficient approaches.
AI.method: Conduct a controlled comparison of contrastive, reconstruction, feature-prediction, and diffusion SSL objectives under matched data, architecture, and compute budgets. Both standalone and jointly trained image-video SSL formulations are evaluated across diverse image and video understanding tasks.
AI.result: DINOv2-style pretraining consistently provides the strongest overall performance under limited resources. Combining DINOv2 with video SSL objectives like VideoMAE substantially improves image classification and segmentation but degrades video tracking and camera-pose estimation, revealing a tradeoff between semantic and geometric representation learning.
AI.conclusion: Combining image and video SSL objectives can be beneficial in resource-limited settings, but there is a need for improved methods that better balance semantic, temporal, and geometric supervision.

title: SketchSense: Learning to Interpret Imperfect Sketch Guidance for Image Inpainting
summary: Sketch-guided image inpainting provides intuitive structural control, yet real sketches often mix reliable global intent with locally crowded, displaced, incomplete, or deliberately unconventional strokes. Existing approaches typically either retain the input sketch as a fixed condition throughout denoising or refine it into a clean structure before RGB synthesis. The former assumes uniformly reliable strokes and can propagate local errors throughout generation; the latter must resolve ambiguous structure before emerging appearance and semantic context become available. We propose SketchSense, a framework that interprets imperfect sketch guidance by synchronously denoising interacting RGB and structure streams. Bidirectional Attention Fusion couples appearance generation with structural recovery, producing a refined structure that exposes the model's evolving sketch interpretation. A phrase-level objective aligns the semantic grounding of the two streams. Sketch-Aware Spatial Regulation further adapts sketch use to local generation states by modulating attention and the fusion process, while an optional signed prior injects preserve-versus-correct intent into feature representations and attention behavior. Experiments on natural and structurally complex imagery show substantial gains over existing methods in both restoration quality and structural fidelity.

AI.tldr: SketchSense is a framework for sketch-guided image inpainting that synchronously denoises interacting RGB and structure streams, using bidirectional attention fusion, phrase-level semantic alignment, and sketch-aware spatial regulation to robustly handle imperfect real-world sketches.
AI.motivation: Real-world sketches often mix reliable global intent with locally imperfect strokes (crowded, displaced, incomplete, or unconventional). Existing methods either treat sketches as fixed conditions throughout denoising (propagating local errors) or refine them into clean structures before RGB synthesis (resolving ambiguity prematurely without semantic context).
AI.method: SketchSense synchronously denoises interacting RGB and structure streams. Key components: (1) Bidirectional Attention Fusion couples appearance generation with structural recovery for evolving sketch interpretation; (2) a phrase-level objective aligns semantic grounding between streams; (3) Sketch-Aware Spatial Regulation adapts sketch usage to local generation states via attention and fusion modulation; (4) an optional signed prior encodes preserve-versus-correct intent into features and attention.
AI.result: Experiments on natural and structurally complex imagery show substantial gains over existing methods in both restoration quality and structural fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Synchronously denoising structure and appearance streams, with bidirectional information flow and context-aware sketch adaptation, enables robust handling of imperfect sketch guidance in inpainting.

title: Fidelity-Constrained Anchoring for Black-Box Denoisers
comment: 5 pages, 5 figures. Supplementary material is available as an ancillary file
summary: We propose a fidelity-constrained framework that anchors the output of a black-box denoiser to its input without retraining and with little additional computation. The method linearly blends the denoised image with the input and selects the maximum blending factor that satisfies a prescribed local fidelity constraint using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) or Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). For PSNR control, a closed-form solution is obtained under a local constant-blending assumption. For SSIM control, we derive a tractable formulation based on inverse SSIM under the same assumption and solve it efficiently using iterative root finding. Experiments on DIV2K images with synthetic Gaussian noise and outputs from Real-ESRGAN and a non-local means denoiser show that the proposed anchoring strategy provides effective fidelity control while balancing denoising performance and statistical naturalness, as measured by the excess kurtosis of residual noise. In particular, SSIM-based anchoring yields more consistent behavior across noise levels than PSNR-based anchoring.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a fidelity-constrained framework that anchors the output of a black-box denoiser to its input by linearly blending the denoised image with the original input. The method selects the maximum blending factor satisfying a local fidelity constraint measured by PSNR or SSIM, offering closed-form solutions for PSNR and iterative root-finding for SSIM, without retraining.
AI.motivation: Black-box denoisers often produce outputs that deviate from the input in ways users may not want, and there is no existing lightweight, retraining-free method to enforce fidelity constraints on arbitrary denoisers.
AI.method: The framework linearly blends the denoised image with the input and selects the maximum blending factor that satisfies a prescribed local fidelity constraint. For PSNR control, a closed-form solution is derived under a local constant-blending assumption. For SSIM control, an inverse SSIM formulation is solved via iterative root finding.
AI.result: Experiments on DIV2K images with synthetic Gaussian noise and outputs from Real-ESRGAN and non-local means denoiser show effective fidelity control while balancing denoising performance and statistical naturalness. SSIM-based anchoring yields more consistent behavior across noise levels than PSNR-based anchoring.
AI.conclusion: The proposed anchoring strategy provides effective, lightweight fidelity control for black-box denoisers, with SSIM-based anchoring offering more consistent performance across varying noise levels.

title: HPSD: Hybrid-Policy Self-Distillation for Text-Image-to-Video Diffusion Models
summary: Text-Image-to-Video (TI2V) models are an emerging unified architecture, where a single model simultaneously supports text-to-video (T2V) and image-to-video (I2V) generation. Given a high-quality first frame or a detailed textual prompt, TI2V models unlock substantially better visual quality than their T2V mode, raising a natural question: can the capability elicited by such privileged conditions be internalized into the model's own base generation ability? A common approach toward this goal is model self-distillation. However, the most straightforward solution, supervised fine-tuning, follows an off-policy strategy: its supervision is confined to teacher-generated endpoints from a fixed offline distribution rather than student-visited states, lacking precise correction tailored to the evolving policy. Recent on-policy distillation methods instead suffer from condition-state mismatch, where supervision is steered toward the given first frame instead of the student's actual content, misleading the correction. To achieve self-distillation that absorbs the teacher's privileged prior while retaining precise policy correction, in this work, we propose Hybrid-Policy Self-Distillation (HPSD), a novel self-distillation framework where a single TI2V model acts as both teacher and student under different conditions: the teacher operates in TI2V mode with a high-quality first frame and an enhanced prompt, while the student runs in the base T2V mode with only the vanilla prompt. Specifically, the student inherits off-policy teacher trajectory points as anchors, locally refines them toward its own policy, and finally receives velocity-level supervision on these self-generated roll-outs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HPSD significantly improves T2V performance while also delivering notable TI2V gains, effectively strengthening the model's base generation ability.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Hybrid-Policy Self-Distillation (HPSD), a framework where a single Text-Image-to-Video (TI2V) model acts as both teacher (in TI2V mode with privileged conditions) and student (in T2V mode with base conditions), improving the model's base text-to-video generation ability while also benefiting image-to-video performance.
AI.motivation: TI2V models achieve significantly better visual quality than their T2V mode when given privileged conditions (high-quality first frame or detailed prompt). The authors ask whether this privileged capability can be internalized into the model's own base generation ability. However, existing approaches fail: supervised fine-tuning is off-policy (only teaches from fixed offline teacher outputs without correcting student-visited states), and on-policy distillation suffers from condition-state mismatch (supervision steered toward the given first frame instead of the student's actual content).
AI.method: HPSD is a self-distillation framework where a single TI2V model serves as both teacher and student under different conditions. The teacher operates in TI2V mode with a high-quality first frame and enhanced prompt, while the student runs in base T2V mode with only the vanilla prompt. The student inherits off-policy teacher trajectory points as anchors, locally refines them toward its own policy, and receives velocity-level supervision on these self-generated roll-outs—hybridizing off-policy and on-policy supervision to avoid their respective pitfalls.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that HPSD significantly improves T2V performance while also delivering notable TI2V gains, effectively strengthening the model's base generation ability.
AI.conclusion: By hybridizing off-policy and on-policy self-distillation strategies, HPSD successfully internalizes the privileged capabilities elicited by TI2V conditions into the model's base T2V generation ability, overcoming the limitations of both pure supervised fine-tuning and existing on-policy distillation methods.

title: NARU: A Benchmark for NARrative Evolution and Cultural Nuance Understanding in Japanese Extreme Long Video
comment: Yuheng Huang and Jianlang Chen contributed equally to this work. More details available on the project's website https://ma-labo.github.io/naru/ and https://infinimind.io/en/company/news/2026/narubench-release
summary: Long-form video understanding encompasses tasks that go beyond retrieving isolated events, including tracking an evolving narrative and interpreting social meaning that may remain implicit. However, existing benchmarks rarely evaluate these capabilities jointly, particularly in high-context, non-English media. To address this gap, we introduce NARU, a benchmark designed to evaluate Narrative evolution and Reasoning on cultural Understanding in Japanese long-form video. NARU consists of 1,481 questions grounded in 155 videos totaling 146.8 hours, spanning four narrative and five cultural dimensions. To construct the benchmark at this scale, we propose a hierarchical memory-based annotation pipeline that transforms raw video into structured event, narrative, and cultural annotations, then generates questions via task-oriented synthesis and iterative shortcut removal. The construction process includes two native-speaker verification stages involving 68 annotators. Evaluations across eight model configurations reveal substantial limitations in both long-range narrative integration and culturally grounded reasoning. By exposing these persistent gaps, NARU offers a systematic testing ground for developing MLLMs capable of reliably interpreting long-form, high-context video.

AI.tldr: NARU is a benchmark for evaluating narrative evolution and cultural understanding in Japanese long-form videos, comprising 1,481 questions from 155 videos (146.8 hours), built via a hierarchical memory-based annotation pipeline with 68 native-speaker annotators, revealing substantial limitations in MLLMs for long-range narrative integration and culturally grounded reasoning.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks rarely evaluate long-form video understanding that jointly tracks evolving narratives and interprets implicit social meaning, particularly in high-context, non-English media like Japanese content.
AI.method: Introduces NARU benchmark with 1,481 questions across 155 videos (146.8 hours), spanning four narrative and five cultural dimensions. Proposes a hierarchical memory-based annotation pipeline that converts raw video into structured event, narrative, and cultural annotations, then generates questions via task-oriented synthesis and iterative shortcut removal, with two native-speaker verification stages involving 68 annotators.
AI.result: Evaluations across eight model configurations reveal substantial limitations in both long-range narrative integration and culturally grounded reasoning, exposing persistent gaps in current MLLMs.
AI.conclusion: NARU provides a systematic testing ground for developing MLLMs capable of reliably interpreting long-form, high-context video, addressing a critical gap in current evaluation practices.

title: UniCon-Former: Unified Convolution Transformer is All You Need for Hand Gesture Recognition
summary: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) capture local features efficiently but struggle with global context due to their limited receptive field. On the other hand, transformers effectively capture global dependencies through self-attention but suffer from high redundancy and computational costs. Thus, to leverage the advantages of both CNNs and transformers, we propose a unified model (UniCon-Former) that aims to provide robust and efficient performance on dynamic hand gesture recognition. The unified approach helps the model to learn both local and global features. At the beginning of each transformer stage, the convolution projections help in decreasing the dimension of the input vectors of the transformer block. This creates a pyramidal structure at each transformer stage. These features enable the UniCon-Former to reduce resource usage than vanilla transformers, making it flexible for learning multi-scale and high-resolution features, which is required in hand gesture recognition. We have performed experiments with NVGesture and Briareo datasets and achieved state-of-the-art results with fewer parameters and MACs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes UniCon-Former, a unified model combining CNNs and transformers for dynamic hand gesture recognition. The model uses convolution projections at the beginning of each transformer stage to reduce input dimensions, creating a pyramidal structure that captures both local and global features while reducing computational costs compared to vanilla transformers. It achieves state-of-the-art results on NVGesture and Briareo datasets with fewer parameters and MACs.
AI.motivation: CNNs capture local features but suffer from limited receptive fields, while transformers capture global context but are computationally expensive and redundant. The authors aim to combine the strengths of both architectures for robust and efficient hand gesture recognition.
AI.method: The proposed unified model (UniCon-Former) integrates CNNs and transformers by using convolution projections at the start of each transformer stage to downscale input vectors, creating a pyramidal structure that enables multi-scale and high-resolution feature learning while reducing resource usage.
AI.result: Experiments on NVGesture and Briareo datasets achieve state-of-the-art results with fewer parameters and MACs (multiply-accumulate operations) compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The unified CNN-transformer approach effectively balances local and global feature learning, delivering robust and efficient performance for dynamic hand gesture recognition while being more resource-efficient than vanilla transformers.

title: Reliability analysis for BraTS-GoAT segmentation: a controlled robustness study of deep-ensemble uncertainty
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Conditionally accepted at MICCAI 2026 BraTS-GoAT challenge workshop. Code: https://github.com/riyashet-hds/brats-goat-reliability
summary: Deep networks segment brain tumours accurately in-distribution, but can fail silently when the input differs from their training data. That risk is central to clinical deployment and is the premise of the BraTS-GoAT generalizability task. We ask not only how well a model segments, but whether its uncertainty knows when it is wrong. On BraTS-GoAT (Task 3) we train a 5-fold cross-validated nnU-Net baseline (one held-out prediction per case) and a 3-seed deep ensemble. Both are evaluated for calibration and error detection on a per-region relevant mask, aggregated per case. In-distribution the 3-seed ensemble improves modestly over the already strong single model on the same held-out split, with the clearest gain in calibration. The separation appears under shift. In a controlled robustness study using graded synthetic corruptions as a proxy for acquisition shift, the single model's confidence stays flat while its accuracy and calibration degrade. Inter-member disagreement instead rises steeply, about a quarter to a third above the clean condition, several times the single model's response. On the official validation leaderboard the 5-fold ensemble of those folds attains whole-tumour Dice 0.87. The generalization gap is concentrated on the harder regions, with a characteristic failure of missing small, satellite lesions on unseen cohorts. In the synthetic study, disagreement among the 3-seed members is a more sensitive case-level indicator of acquisition shift than single-model confidence. Its per-voxel error localisation weakens as severity grows. The contribution is a rigorous, honest reliability comparison rather than a claim that any one uncertainty method dominates.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates deep learning segmentation models for brain tumours under distribution shift, comparing a 5-fold cross-validated nnU-Net baseline against a 3-seed deep ensemble on the BraTS-GoAT Task 3. The ensemble shows modest in-distribution gains but markedly better uncertainty calibration and shift sensitivity—inter-member disagreement rises steeply under synthetic corruption, making it a more sensitive indicator of acquisition shift than single-model confidence.
AI.motivation: Deep networks segment brain tumours accurately in-distribution but can fail silently under distribution shift, which is a central risk for clinical deployment. The paper addresses not just segmentation performance but whether model uncertainty can reliably signal when the model is wrong, as formalized in the BraTS-GoAT generalizability task.
AI.method: A 5-fold cross-validated nnU-Net baseline (with one held-out prediction per case) and a 3-seed deep ensemble are trained and evaluated on BraTS-GoAT Task 3. Calibration and error detection are assessed on a per-region relevant mask aggregated per case. A controlled robustness study uses graded synthetic corruptions as a proxy for acquisition shift to compare single-model confidence vs. ensemble disagreement.
AI.result: In-distribution, the 3-seed ensemble improves modestly over the single model with clearest gains in calibration. Under synthetic shift, single-model confidence stays flat while accuracy/calibration degrade, whereas ensemble disagreement rises ~25-33% above the clean condition. On the official validation leaderboard, the 5-fold ensemble achieves whole-tumour Dice 0.87. Generalization gaps concentrate on harder regions, particularly small satellite lesions. Disagreement is a more sensitive case-level shift indicator, though per-voxel error localisation weakens with severity.
AI.conclusion: The contribution is a rigorous, honest reliability comparison rather than a claim that any single uncertainty method dominates—ensemble disagreement is more sensitive to acquisition shift at the case level, while both approaches have limitations in per-voxel error localisation under increasing severity.

title: CoverPrune: Coverage-Driven Token Pruning for 3D VLMs via Optimal Transport
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026 as an Oral Presentation
summary: While 3D Vision-Language Models (3D VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable spatial reasoning capabilities, they suffer from massive visual token counts that create severe computational bottlenecks during inference. Existing token pruning methods primarily rely on diversity-based selection, discarding similar tokens to maximize dispersion. However, in 3D environments, this approach frequently drops representative prototype tokens in favor of outliers, breaking the multi-view consistencies and geometric structures essential for spatial reasoning. In this paper, we propose a paradigm shift for 3D VLM token pruning: from maximizing diversity to preserving visual evidence coverage. We introduce CoverPrune, a training-free framework that formulates inference-time token pruning as an Optimal Transport (OT) problem. To overcome the intractable combinatorial subset selection inherent in this formulation, we design the Feature-Spatial-Temporal (FST) transport cost and target capacity, along with an efficient Spatial-Guided Greedy Selection (SGS) algorithm to approximate the OT objective. Furthermore, we propose CoverPrune-Lite, an accelerated variant utilizing spatially structured local matching for minimal overhead. Extensive experiments across multiple 3D visual-spatial reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that our methods achieve state-of-the-art token efficiency, maintaining robust reasoning performance even under highly aggressive pruning budgets. Visit our project website at https://github.com/Brucess/CoverPrune.

AI.tldr: CoverPrune is a training-free token pruning framework for 3D Vision-Language Models that shifts from diversity-based token selection to preserving visual evidence coverage, formulated as an Optimal Transport problem with an efficient Spatial-Guided Greedy Selection algorithm, achieving state-of-the-art token efficiency while maintaining robust spatial reasoning performance.
AI.motivation: 3D VLMs suffer from massive visual token counts creating severe computational bottlenecks during inference. Existing diversity-based token pruning methods discard similar tokens to maximize dispersion, but in 3D environments this frequently drops representative prototype tokens in favor of outliers, breaking multi-view consistencies and geometric structures essential for spatial reasoning.
AI.method: The paper proposes CoverPrune, a training-free framework formulating inference-time token pruning as an Optimal Transport (OT) problem. It designs the Feature-Spatial-Temporal (FST) transport cost and target capacity, plus an efficient Spatial-Guided Greedy Selection (SGS) algorithm to approximate the OT objective. A faster variant, CoverPrune-Lite, uses spatially structured local matching for minimal overhead.
AI.result: Extensive experiments across multiple 3D visual-spatial reasoning benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art token efficiency, with robust reasoning performance maintained even under highly aggressive pruning budgets.
AI.conclusion: The paradigm shift from maximizing diversity to preserving visual evidence coverage enables more effective and efficient token pruning for 3D VLMs, preserving the spatial reasoning capabilities even under aggressive computational constraints.

title: Reasoning for Social Audio-Visual Question Answering: Where Do We Stand?
comment: Accepted at HCMIW ECCV workshop. Code available here: https://github.com/koenv759/VanillaSFT
summary: Training Multimodal Large Language Models for audio-visual social understanding is a crucial step toward embodied social intelligence. Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has become the dominant approach, with HumanOmniV2 and its IntentBench benchmark as a prominent reference point. In this context, we report three findings. First, IntentBench is highly noisy: $\sim$7% of questions are broken and $\sim$23% are trivially answerable without the video input. We remove the affected questions and release Intentbench-Prime. Second, current reasoning approaches are expensive and surprisingly ineffective. A simple Vanilla SFT baseline matches or outperforms existing reasoning methods across three benchmarks at a fraction of the cost, establishing it as an essential baseline for evaluating novel fine-tuning techniques. Third, our analysis reveals that substantial priors can be learned solely from the text modality and that using a textual caption instead of the video yields performance on par with Vanilla SFT. These surprising findings reveal the limitations of current MLLMs when it comes to social understanding. IntentBench-Prime, Vanilla SFT model, and code are publicly available.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates multimodal LLMs for audio-visual social understanding, finding three key issues: (1) the IntentBench benchmark is noisy with broken/trivially answerable questions, (2) simple Vanilla SFT outperforms expensive chain-of-thought reasoning methods, and (3) models rely heavily on text-only priors, achieving comparable performance with captions instead of video. The authors release IntentBench-Prime and a Vanilla SFT baseline.
AI.motivation: To advance embodied social intelligence, there is a need for reliable training and evaluation of multimodal large language models for audio-visual social understanding. The authors question the effectiveness of current chain-of-thought reasoning approaches and benchmark quality, challenging the dominant paradigm.
AI.method: The authors conduct a systematic evaluation of IntentBench and existing reasoning methods. They filter noisy questions to create IntentBench-Prime, compare a simple Vanilla SFT baseline against expensive reasoning approaches, and perform ablations using text-only captions versus video input to isolate modality contributions.
AI.result: IntentBench contains ~7% broken questions and ~23% trivially answerable without video. Vanilla SFT matches or outperforms reasoning methods at lower cost. Text captions alone yield performance on par with Vanilla SFT with video, revealing heavy reliance on text priors.
AI.conclusion: Current MLLMs have significant limitations in social understanding, and the field's reliance on complex reasoning and video-heavy benchmarks may be misguided. The released IntentBench-Prime and Vanilla SFT baseline establish a more rigorous foundation for future work.

title: GeoCache: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View Texture Diffusion via Geometric Delta Transport
summary: Geometry-conditioned multi-view diffusion enables high-quality 3D texture generation, but its repeated per-view denoiser evaluations introduce substantial computational cost. Existing training-free accelerators primarily exploit temporal redundancy by reusing computation across denoising steps. In multi-view texturing, however, skipping a step also removes the cross-view interaction that continually aligns different observations of the same surface, leading to rapidly degraded consistency and fidelity. Our analysis identifies a complementary source of redundancy: although intermediate features remain view-specific, geometrically corresponding surface points exhibit transferable evolution in their predicted clean signals. Based on this observation, we introduce \gc{}, a training-free plugin that evaluates a rotating subset of anchor views and transports their geometry-aligned per-step $\xz$ updates to the remaining views. Periodic full-view computation controls accumulated error, while sampler-consistent reconstruction preserves the denoising trajectory. \gc{} requires neither retraining nor architectural modification and uses the position maps already available in geometry-conditioned texturing pipelines. Across Hunyuan3D-2.1, SyncMVD, and MVPainter, \gc{} achieves a stronger speed--fidelity trade-off than temporal caches and step reduction at operating points above $2\times$. On Hunyuan3D-2.1, it delivers a $2.21\times$ denoiser-loop speedup with an MV-LPIPS of 0.0293 and an MV-PSNR of 33.60 dB, providing the best fidelity among all tested methods above $2\times$. The same transferred configuration reaches the highest speedup and lowest FLOPs on SyncMVD, while \gc{} achieves the lowest FLOPs and best fidelity among the accelerated methods on MVPainter. These results establish cross-view geometry as an effective acceleration axis for multi-view texture diffusion.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces GC, a training-free acceleration plugin for geometry-conditioned multi-view texture diffusion. Instead of exploiting temporal redundancy across denoising steps (which harms cross-view consistency), GC evaluates a rotating subset of anchor views and transports geometry-aligned per-step clean-signal updates to remaining views. It achieves 2.21x denoiser-loop speedup on Hunyuan3D-2.1 with strong fidelity (MV-LPIPS 0.0293, MV-PSNR 33.60 dB), and consistently outperforms temporal caches and step reduction across three diffusion models.
AI.motivation: Multi-view diffusion for 3D texture generation is computationally expensive due to repeated per-view denoiser evaluations. Existing training-free accelerators exploit temporal redundancy by skipping denoising steps, but this removes cross-view interaction needed to maintain surface consistency across views, causing degraded fidelity. The paper identifies that skipping computation (not steps) is the right axis: geometrically corresponding surface points across views share transferable evolution in their predicted clean signals.
AI.method: GC is a training-free plugin that: (1) evaluates a rotating subset of anchor views each step; (2) transports geometry-aligned per-step clean-signal (xt) updates from anchor views to the remaining views using position maps already available in geometry-conditioned pipelines; (3) periodically performs full-view computation to control accumulated error; (4) uses sampler-consistent reconstruction to preserve the denoising trajectory. No retraining or architectural modification is required.
AI.result: On Hunyuan3D-2.1, GC achieves 2.21x denoiser-loop speedup with MV-LPIPS of 0.0293 and MV-PSNR of 33.60 dB, yielding the best fidelity among all methods above 2x speedup. It reaches the highest speedup and lowest FLOPs on SyncMVD with the transferred configuration, and achieves the lowest FLOPs with the best fidelity among accelerated methods on MVPainter.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes cross-view geometry as an effective acceleration axis for multi-view texture diffusion, complementing temporal redundancy exploitation. GC demonstrates that geometric correspondence between views provides a transferable computation-sharing opportunity that avoids the consistency degradation caused by step skipping, delivering a stronger speed-fidelity trade-off than existing temporal caches and step reduction.

title: How Good are Foundation Models in Longitudinal MRI Disease Progression Reasoning?
comment: Accepted at MICCAI 2026 (Early Accept). 11 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables
summary: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) interpretation is fundamental to clinical decision-making, requiring radiologists to integrate multi-view anatomical planes across sequential timepoints while precisely localizing interval changes. However, existing vision-language benchmarks remain confined to single-timepoint, single-view interpretation, failing to capture the temporal-spatial reasoning essential to radiologic practice. We introduce the Time-Aware Multi-View MRI Benchmark, an evaluation framework unifying multi-view anatomical input, temporal reasoning across longitudinal scans, and structured localization guidance. The benchmark comprises 3,920 expert-verified question-answer pairs derived from 890 patients across over 3,200 longitudinal MRI timepoints, drawn from seven clinical cohorts covering glioblastoma, neurodegeneration, vestibular schwannoma, and brain metastases, in open-ended, multiple-choice, and binary formats, requiring models to identify anatomical regions of maximal change, characterize progression across sequences and views, and provide structured guidance specifying boundaries, imaging features, and confounders. Experiments across 16 vision-language models reveal moderate temporal alignment but systematic failure on change direction recognition and volumetric quantification, while multi-view inputs improve spatial localization yet degrade temporal reasoning in compact architectures. Our benchmark provides a systematic framework for evaluating progression tracking, interval change localization, and temporal ordering, which are essential for clinical deployment. Code, evaluation splits, and the dataset are available at: https://github.com/wafaAlghallabi/Time-Aware-MRI.

AI.tldr: Introduces the Time-Aware Multi-View MRI Benchmark, a new evaluation framework with 3,920 expert-verified QA pairs from 890 patients across 3,200+ longitudinal MRI timepoints, unifying multi-view anatomical input, temporal reasoning, and structured localization. Testing 16 VLMs reveals moderate temporal alignment but systematic failures in change direction recognition and volumetric quantification.
AI.motivation: Existing vision-language benchmarks for MRI are limited to single-timepoint, single-view interpretation, failing to capture the temporal-spatial reasoning that radiologists actually use when tracking interval changes across longitudinal scans and multiple anatomical planes.
AI.method: The benchmark comprises 3,920 expert-verified QA pairs derived from 890 patients across 3,200+ longitudinal MRI timepoints from seven clinical cohorts (glioblastoma, neurodegeneration, vestibular schwannoma, brain metastases), in open-ended, multiple-choice, and binary formats. Tasks require identifying anatomical regions of maximal change, characterizing progression across sequences/views, and providing structured guidance on boundaries, features, and confounders.
AI.result: Experiments across 16 vision-language models show moderate temporal alignment but systematic failure on change direction recognition and volumetric quantification. Multi-view inputs improve spatial localization yet degrade temporal reasoning in compact architectures.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark provides a systematic framework for evaluating progression tracking, interval change localization, and temporal ordering — capabilities essential for clinical deployment of VLMs in radiology.

title: AmalthAI: An Open-Source Computer Vision Platform for Cultural Heritage
summary: Computer vision (CV) and machine learning (ML) offer new tools for cultural heritage (CH) artifact analysis, but the CV/ML pipeline remains largely inaccessible to CH domain experts, who lack the background to configure, train, or assess models. We present AmalthAI, an open-source CV platform that bridges this gap, enabling non-ML CH experts to independently produce and validate archaeologically meaningful findings. The interface covers dataset management, training, and inference for classification, segmentation, and object detection, with Kubeflow and Katib handling scalable training and hyperparameter search. Grad-CAM localizes the image region behind a prediction, and a vision-language model (VLM) adds a text description of it for expert review. Since archaeological data is often state-owned or rights-encumbered and cannot leave institutional custody, AmalthAI's self-hostable deployment ensures sensitive data is kept within premises. We test the platform on an archaeological use case built on a custom dataset of clay textile imprints, where CH experts trained and validated segmentation, and classification models for hypothesis testing. We provide the implementation code at https://github.com/TEXTaiLES/AmalthAI.

AI.tldr: AmalthAI is an open-source computer vision platform designed to make CV/ML pipelines accessible to cultural heritage domain experts who lack ML backgrounds. It provides an end-to-end interface for dataset management, training, and inference (classification, segmentation, object detection) with Kubeflow/Katib for scalable training, Grad-CAM for prediction localization, and a vision-language model for expert review. The platform is self-hostable to address sensitive/rights-encumbered archaeological data, and was validated on a case study involving clay textile imprints where CH experts trained segmentation and classification models.
AI.motivation: Computer vision and machine learning offer powerful tools for cultural heritage artifact analysis, but the CV/ML pipeline is largely inaccessible to CH domain experts who lack the technical background to configure, train, or assess models. There is a gap between the capabilities of CV/ML and the practical needs of CH researchers.
AI.method: The paper presents AmalthAI, an open-source CV platform with an accessible interface covering dataset management, training, and inference for classification, segmentation, and object detection. It uses Kubeflow and Katib for scalable training and hyperparameter search, Grad-CAM to localize image regions behind predictions, and a vision-language model (VLM) to generate text descriptions of predictions for expert review. The platform is self-hostable to keep sensitive archaeological data within institutional premises.
AI.result: The platform was tested on an archaeological use case with a custom dataset of clay textile imprints, where CH experts successfully trained and validated segmentation and classification models for hypothesis testing. The implementation code is publicly available on GitHub.
AI.conclusion: AmalthAI successfully bridges the gap between CV/ML capabilities and CH domain expertise by providing an accessible, self-hostable platform that allows non-ML cultural heritage experts to independently produce and validate archaeologically meaningful findings while respecting data custody constraints.

title: Sign Language Video Synthesis via Loss-Guided Multi-Expert GANs
comment: Preliminary technical report. 19 pages, 8 figures, 4 algorithms
summary: This preliminary technical report presents a framework for sign language video synthesis using a loss-guided multi-expert Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) to enhance communication for individuals with hearing impairments. Three specialized discriminators -- global, hand, and head -- each guide a corresponding expert branch in the generator toward a distinct visual region, enabling implicit feature specialization without explicit diversity losses. To stabilize this multi-discriminator system, whose early-phase training otherwise exhibits chaotic dynamics, we introduce a United Loss consensus mechanism that regularizes each discriminator toward the ensemble average at a 10% weight. Each branch further adopts a dual-pathway convolutional-transformer design with learnable AdaptiveFeatureFusion, balancing the stability of convolutions against the detail of windowed self-attention. The generator is trained using an alternating three-mode schedule (discriminator, holistic generation, branch-specialized generation). On a custom 156GB dataset with a filtered test set that removes easy and repetitive samples, our 0.2B-parameter variant achieves 29.8 PSNR and the 1.3B-parameter variant achieves 30.7 PSNR, with inference VRAM footprints of 1.5 GB and 8 GB respectively, enabling deployment on consumer-grade hardware. Full ablation studies remain ongoing due to the 2-3 month training cycle on a single GPU. The system was showcased at the 2025 Hong Kong Frontier Technology Summit.

AI.tldr: This technical report presents a loss-guided multi-expert GAN framework for sign language video synthesis, featuring three specialized discriminators (global, hand, head) guiding corresponding generator branches, stabilized by a United Loss consensus mechanism, and achieving 29.8-30.7 PSNR on a custom 156GB dataset with consumer-grade hardware compatibility.
AI.motivation: To enhance communication for individuals with hearing impairments by developing sign language video synthesis technology.
AI.method: A multi-expert GAN with three specialized discriminators (global, hand, head) each guiding a generator branch, stabilized by a United Loss consensus mechanism (10% weight toward ensemble average), dual-pathway convolutional-transformer architecture with learnable AdaptiveFeatureFusion, and an alternating three-mode training schedule (discriminator, holistic, branch-specialized generation).
AI.result: Achieves 29.8 PSNR (0.2B params, 1.5GB VRAM) and 30.7 PSNR (1.3B params, 8GB VRAM) on a filtered custom 156GB dataset. Full ablation studies pending due to 2-3 month single-GPU training cycle.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables consumer-grade hardware deployment via compact parameter variants, was showcased at the 2025 Hong Kong Frontier Technology Summit, and requires further ablation validation.

title: Reconstructing Historical Manuscripts through MSI: The Potential of Contrast in Assessing Image Quality and Legibility
comment: 8 pages main paper, 7 pages Supplementary Material
summary: Digital restoration of historical manuscript images aims to improve readability while preserving the authenticity of cultural heritage documents. However, evaluating quality of restored manuscripts remains challenging, where readability is often subjective and expert annotations are scarce. This study investigates the suitability of contrast-based image quality measures to assess quality and legibility of reconstructed manuscript images from multi-spectral imaging. Two experiments were conducted with publicly-available data sets, facilitating manual quality scores by experts and full-reference image quality measures as reference evaluations. The results show that potential contrast achieves the highest correlation with expert ratings, while contrast-to-noise ratio demonstrates the strongest agreement with full-reference quality measures. Overall, contrast-based measures consistently outperform general image quality measures, demonstrating their potential as objective indicators of manuscript legibility and reconstruction quality.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates contrast-based image quality measures for assessing the quality and legibility of digitally restored historical manuscript images from multi-spectral imaging. Through two experiments using public datasets with expert ratings and full-reference metrics, the authors find that potential contrast correlates best with expert ratings, while contrast-to-noise ratio agrees most strongly with full-reference quality measures, with contrast-based measures consistently outperforming general image quality metrics.
AI.motivation: Evaluating the quality of restored manuscript images is challenging because readability is subjective and expert annotations are scarce. There is a need for objective, automated quality measures that can reliably indicate manuscript legibility and reconstruction quality.
AI.method: The study conducts two experiments using publicly available datasets. It compares contrast-based image quality measures against expert manual quality scores and full-reference image quality measures, assessing correlations between these contrast measures and the reference evaluations.
AI.result: Potential contrast achieves the highest correlation with expert ratings, while contrast-to-noise ratio demonstrates the strongest agreement with full-reference quality measures. Contrast-based measures consistently outperform general image quality measures.
AI.conclusion: Contrast-based measures, particularly potential contrast and contrast-to-noise ratio, can serve as effective objective indicators of manuscript legibility and reconstruction quality in digital restoration of historical manuscripts.

title: When Is a Task Vector Enough? An Empirical Theory of Implicit Multimodal ICL
comment: Accepted by Empirical Theory in Representation Learning @ ECCV 2026, Oral
